requirements.title: TimelineItem is the single persisted unit of a conversation, with id, optional turnID, date and a tagged content union
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:4-15 struct TimelineItem - Codable, Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable; fields id: String, turnID: UUID?, date: Date, content: Content; init defaults id = UUID().uuidString and date = .now
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:17-26 enum Content - the eight cases the timeline can hold
requirements.preconditions: A thread document is being built in memory or decoded from disk.
requirements.action: The runtime appends or decodes a timeline item.
requirements.expected_result: Every item carries exactly four stored fields: id (String, defaulting to a fresh UUID string), turnID (UUID or null), date (Date, defaulting to now) and content, which is exactly one of user, assistant, reasoning, tool, plan, todos, notice, turnEnd. No other case exists and no other field is stored.
requirements.persistence: Serialized inside ThreadDocument.items under the JSON keys id, turnID, date, content; the content union is encoded by Swift's synthesized enum coding, i.e. a single-key object whose key is the case name.
failure_cases: An item that fails to decode is dropped rather than failing the whole document (see PR-CHAT-019).
requirements.windows_path: A discriminated-union record type in the Windows model layer, serialized with the same key names and the same single-key-object shape for the union, so a thread written by either build round-trips.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture: encode/decode round-trip against a pinned JSON fixture per content case

requirements.title: Attachment identifies a file by path and mime type, is an image when the mime type starts with image/, and hands providers base64 images that are downscaled past 2000 pixels
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:89-97 struct Attachment - id = UUID(), name, path, mimeType; url is URL(fileURLWithPath: path); isImage is mimeType.hasPrefix("image/")

DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:102-111 Attachment.base64Images - `@concurrent`; compactMap over attachments; `guard attachment.isImage, let data = try? Data(contentsOf: attachment.url) else { return nil }`; `let downscaled = downscaledJPEG(data)`; `var sent = attachment`; `if downscaled != nil { sent.mimeType = "image/jpeg" }`; `return (sent, (downscaled ?? data).base64EncodedString())`
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:113-137 `private static let maxPixelSize = 2000` and downscaledJPEG, specified in PR-CHAT-190

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:228-232 `for (image, base64) in await Attachment.base64Images(input.images)` with `"media_type": .string(image.mimeType)`; the other callers are DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:177 and DroppyCode/Services/Providers/OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:1223
requirements.preconditions: A message carries attachments.
requirements.action: The UI or the provider path asks whether an attachment is an image, or asks for the base64 images.
requirements.expected_result: isImage is a literal prefix test on the mimeType string against "image/", never on the file extension. base64Images reads each image's bytes off the main actor and silently skips any attachment whose bytes cannot be read, returning only the pairs that succeeded, in the original order. For each image it tries downscaledJPEG (PR-CHAT-190): when that returns data, the pair carries that JPEG's base64 and a copy of the attachment whose mimeType is "image/jpeg"; otherwise it carries the original bytes' base64 and the attachment unchanged. The stored attachment is never modified; only the returned copy changes.
side_effects: base64Images reads each image file from disk
An image more than 2000 pixels on its longest side is decoded and re-encoded as a JPEG in memory
requirements.persistence: id, name, path and mimeType are persisted with the message.
failure_cases: A file that cannot be read is dropped from the result with no error and no notice.
An image ImageIO cannot read, or whose JPEG encoding fails, is sent with its original bytes and mime type, with no error and no notice.
requirements.windows_path: URL(fileURLWithPath:) becomes a Windows absolute path; the stored path is the platform path as captured. Base64 encoding and any downscaling must run off the UI thread: the source comment records that a photo is megabytes and its string a third larger again. The returned copy's mime type must follow the bytes actually sent (image/jpeg after a downscale), because the Claude session sends it as the image's media_type (ClaudeSession.swift:228-232).
requirements.verification_method: unit with a fixture directory holding one unreadable path, one image at most 2000 pixels on its longest side and one larger image, asserting order, skipped entries, returned bytes and returned mime types
requirements.b2_change: B1 Timeline.swift:99-105 base64Images returned `(attachment, data.base64EncodedString())` -> B2 Timeline.swift:102-111 returns `(sent, (downscaled ?? data).base64EncodedString())`, with `sent.mimeType = "image/jpeg"` whenever `downscaledJPEG(data)` (B2 :120-137) produced a JPEG, so images above maxPixelSize = 2000 (B2 :114) reach providers downscaled. isImage and the silent skip of unreadable files are unchanged.

requirements.title: Tool output is trimmed to a 60000-byte ceiling by replacing the head with a single ellipsis and keeping the last 30000 bytes
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:169 static let outputLimit = 60_000
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:181-189 appendOutput appends then trims; setOutput replaces then trims
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:196-199 trimOutput - guard output.utf8.count > Self.outputLimit; output = "…" + String(output.suffix(Self.outputLimit / 2))
requirements.preconditions: A tool call is streaming or has just received its whole output.
requirements.expected_result: While the output's UTF-8 byte count is at most 60000 it is kept whole. Above that the output becomes the single character U+2026 HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS followed by the last 30000 Characters of the current output. Note that the guard counts UTF-8 bytes while suffix counts Characters, so the trimmed result can still exceed 60000 bytes for non-ASCII output; this is the shipped behavior.
requirements.persistence: The trimmed value is what is stored in the item and written to disk.
requirements.windows_path: Reproduce the byte-count guard and the Character-count suffix exactly, including the unit mismatch. Windows string indices are UTF-16 code units: suffix must be taken over grapheme clusters, not code units, or a surrogate pair is split.
requirements.verification_method: unit with an ASCII case, a CJK case and an emoji case at the boundary

After 250 milliseconds the end is held for a further second and the window's start moves to the block twenty-four from the end of the block list the task captured when it started (or that list's first block), so the window holds the newest twenty-four blocks, which land above the viewport while the reader is already looking at the end; a blank watch is armed and every finished reply's markdown is parsed off the main thread. Each timeline reports its own; this is the union. It flips at most twice per scroll, so a view that reads it re-renders at the start and at the end, never per frame. Motion that has no business running under a moving finger (a progress sweep, a shimmer, a breathing ring) pauses on it and gives the frame back to the scroll.'

requirements.preconditions: One or more timelines report their scrolling.
requirements.action: A timeline starts or stops scrolling, or a reporting timeline goes away without withdrawing.
requirements.expected_result: The shared flag is true exactly while at least one timeline is on record as scrolling, so a settings pane being scrolled suppresses motion app-wide. The flag is written only when it actually changes, so readers re-render at the start and the end of a scroll and never per frame. While any timeline is on record a single watchdog task wakes every 2 seconds, asks each recorded reporter whether it is still scrolling, and drops every timeline whose reporter has gone away or answers no; it then re-publishes the union and, once nothing is left, clears itself and returns. At most one watchdog exists at a time. Clearing the set by an explicit stop cancels the watchdog immediately rather than waiting for its next pass.

DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:116-119 the doc comment: a JPEG of the image at no more than maxPixelSize on its longest side, or nil for an image already that small or one ImageIO cannot read, which keeps its own bytes; the thumbnail is generated with its transform applied, so an orientation flag does not reach the provider as a sideways photo

DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:120-125 `guard let source = CGImageSourceCreateWithData(data as CFData, nil), let properties = CGImageSourceCopyPropertiesAtIndex(source, 0, nil) as? [CFString: Any], let width = properties[kCGImagePropertyPixelWidth] as? Int, let height = properties[kCGImagePropertyPixelHeight] as? Int, max(width, height) > maxPixelSize else { return nil }`

DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:126-130 `kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways: true`, `kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform: true`, `kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize: maxPixelSize`

DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:131-136 `CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex(source, 0, options as CFDictionary)`; `CGImageDestinationCreateWithData(output, "public.jpeg" as CFString, 1, nil)`; `CGImageDestinationAddImage(destination, thumbnail, [kCGImageDestinationLossyCompressionQuality: 0.8] as CFDictionary)`; `guard CGImageDestinationFinalize(destination) else { return nil }`; `return output as Data`
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:98-111 base64Images calls it once per image and marks the returned copy image/jpeg when it returns data (PR-CHAT-005)
requirements.preconditions: A message with image attachments is being sent through the ACP, Claude or OpenAI-compatible session.
requirements.expected_result: The pixel width and height are read from the properties of the image at index 0. If either cannot be read, or the longer of the two is 2000 or less, nothing is re-encoded and the original bytes are used; an image exactly 2000 pixels on its longest side is sent as it is. Otherwise a thumbnail of the image at index 0 is created from the full image (always, not from an embedded thumbnail), with its orientation transform applied, no more than 2000 pixels on its longest side, and encoded as a single-image JPEG (public.jpeg) at lossy compression quality 0.8. If the thumbnail or the JPEG cannot be produced, the original bytes are used.
side_effects: The image is decoded and re-encoded in memory; nothing is written to disk
requirements.persistence: None; the attachment file on disk and the stored Attachment are untouched.
failure_cases: An image that cannot be read or decoded falls back to its original bytes and mime type, silently.
A failed JPEG encode falls back to the original bytes and mime type, silently.
requirements.windows_path: Windows needs a decoder that reads the pixel dimensions and the orientation flag, an orientation-aware resize to at most 2000 pixels on the longest side that keeps the aspect ratio, and a JPEG encoder at quality 0.8 (for example Windows Imaging Component). The comparison is strictly greater than 2000.
requirements.verification_method: unit over fixture images: 2000 by 1000 (original bytes and mime), 2001 by 1000 and 4000 by 3000 (JPEG, longest side at most 2000, mime image/jpeg), a photo with a rotating orientation flag (upright JPEG) and a corrupt file (original bytes)

requirements.title: Once anchored, the lazy window keeps its oldest block by identity, so blocks appended at the end never evict an older row
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:77-81 `@State private var windowStartID: String?` with the comment: where the lazy window begins, the id of its oldest block; the window runs from that block to the end, so a block appended at the end never evicts an older row from the stack; only loading history or a jump moves the start; nil until the thread anchors, when the newest `firstPaint` blocks are the window

DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:158-163 `let startIndex = windowStartIndex(in: blocks)`; `let hidden = startIndex`; `let visible = startIndex == 0 ? blocks : Array(blocks[startIndex...])`
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:273-278 windowStartIndex - `if let windowStartID, let index = blocks.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == windowStartID }) { return index }`
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:229, :267 and :716 the only writes to windowStartID: a jump above the window, a history load and nil on a thread switch
requirements.preconditions: A thread is open and its window start has been set by the initial load, a page load or a minimap jump.
requirements.action: New blocks are appended at the end of the conversation (a reply streams in, a tool runs, a turn ends).
requirements.expected_result: The first rendered block stays the same block and the rendered count grows by the appended blocks; no row that was visible a frame ago is removed from the top. The hidden count on the earlier-messages pill is the start block's index, so appending does not change it. The start only moves back (a history load or a jump) until the thread is switched, which clears the anchor.
failure_cases: An anchor whose block has left the conversation falls back to the newest three blocks (PR-CHAT-192).
requirements.windows_path: Store the window start as the oldest block's id, not a count or a suffix length, and derive its index from the current block list on every pass.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test: open a long thread, wait for the 24-block window, stream three more blocks and assert the first rendered block id and the pill's hidden count are unchanged

requirements.title: With no anchor, or an anchor whose block is gone, the lazy window is the newest three blocks
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:270-278 windowStartIndex - the doc comment says a start whose block has left the conversation falls back to the newest firstPaint blocks; `return max(0, blocks.count - TimelineWindow.firstPaint)` when no block matches windowStartID
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:1804-1811 `static let firstPaint = 3`, `static let initial = 24`
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:713-720 a thread switch sets `windowStartID = nil`

DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:257-268 loadEarlier - with count TimelineWindow.initial the target is `count.map { max(0, blocks.count - $0) }`, the block count minus 24 floored at zero, and `guard target < start else { return }` leaves the window unanchored when that target is not before the fallback start

DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:595-603 `.task(id: runtime.threadID)` inside timelineScroll(blocks:...) sleeps 250 ms and then calls `loadEarlier(in: blocks, to: TimelineWindow.initial)` with the `blocks` its closure captured
requirements.preconditions: windowStartID is nil (a thread just opened or switched to, before the 250 ms load anchors it) or names a block that is no longer in the conversation.
requirements.expected_result: The window is the newest min(3, block count) blocks, and the earlier-messages pill counts the rest as hidden. While unanchored, an appended block moves the window along with the end, so it stays the newest three. A thread whose block list, as captured by the thread task when it started (the `blocks` passed to timelineScroll when `.task(id: runtime.threadID)` began), holds three blocks or fewer stays unanchored after the 250 ms load, because that load computes its target (that captured count minus 24, floored at zero) and the fallback start from the captured list, and the target is not before the start; it stays so until a page load or a jump sets the anchor. A stale anchor is not cleared by the lookup: it simply stops matching.
requirements.windows_path: Compute the fallback on every pass rather than storing it, and leave a stale anchor id in place, exactly as the source does.
requirements.verification_method: unit over the window-start function with a nil anchor, a present anchor and a removed anchor; interaction test opening a two-block thread and streaming two more blocks, asserting the pill appears with 1 hidden

requirements.title: Dragging the knob snaps to the nearest stop and fires an alignment haptic on each change
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:801-818 DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) - the first change sets dragX inside .spring(response: 0.22, dampingFraction: 0.8), later changes set it directly; nearestStop is taken and, when it differs from the index, the index is written and NSHapticFeedbackManager performs .alignment at .now; onEnded clears dragX inside .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.78)
DroppyCode/App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:833-836 nearestStop = min(count - 1, max(0, Int(((x - inset) / step).rounded())))
requirements.preconditions: A slider with two or more stops.
requirements.action: The user presses anywhere on the track and drags.
requirements.expected_result: A press with no movement already acts, because the minimum distance is zero: pressed on the track away from the knob, the knob springs to the pointer; pressed on the knob (within its 24 px radius of its drawn centre), it lifts to 1.06x where it is and never slides sideways (OD-0090). The knob follows the pointer, clamped to the insets, keeping the grip's offset when it was pressed on the knob (the source's knob centres on the pointer), and the selected index is the nearest stop to the knob's centre by rounding, so it changes as the centre passes the midpoint between two stops (OD-0090; the source rounds the pointer's position, which is the same except for the grip's offset). On the press the knob springs (response 0.22, damping 0.8): it lifts to 1.06x always, and slides to the pointer when it was pressed on the track; on release it springs onto the nearest stop and back to 1x (response 0.32, damping 0.78). The springs are the locked page's physical spring (work/design/jewel-knob-locked/jewel-knob.html:447-452: stiffness (2 pi / response)^2, damping 4 pi z / response), integrated in steps of at most 4 ms; a drawn frame moves them by the time since the last drawn frame, at most 50 ms (:813), so after a stall the knob goes on from where it was; the knob's drawn centre may pass either end's stop by at most 3 px while it springs (:586). Each index change fires an alignment haptic.
side_effects: Haptic feedback on each stop crossed
requirements.persistence: Through the binding, the thread's effort and the model preference.
failure_cases: count <= 1 or step <= 0: nearestStop returns 0.
requirements.cancellation: A cancelled gesture or a lost pointer capture releases the knob exactly as a release does: it springs onto the nearest stop and back to 1x (OD-0090; work/design/jewel-knob-locked/jewel-knob.html:556-557 pointerup, pointercancel and lostpointercapture all run the same release; the source leaves dragX set until the next gesture, with no cancellation handler).
requirements.windows_path: The springs are the locked page's, whose numbers are the source's (response 0.22 s, damping 0.8 held; 0.32 s, 0.78 released), applied as in expected_result; the drag keeps the grip's offset and rounds the knob's centre to the nearest stop (OD-0090). Haptics have no Windows equivalent and are dropped silently, never substituted with sound (port_impacts X8(e)).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test dragging across all stops

requirements.title: A video thumbnail frame is grabbed half a second in, off the main actor, at twice the point size with the track transform applied
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:146-158 `/// One video frame off the main actor, so opening a movie never stalls drawing.` with `static func thumbnail(for path: String, pointSize: CGFloat) async -> CGImage? { await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) { let pixels = Int((pointSize * 2).rounded(.up)); let asset = AVURLAsset(url: URL(fileURLWithPath: path)); let generator = AVAssetImageGenerator(asset: asset); generator.appliesPreferredTrackTransform = true; generator.maximumSize = CGSize(width: pixels, height: pixels); /* A beat in, so a black first frame does not become the thumbnail. */ let time = CMTime(seconds: 0.5, preferredTimescale: 600); return try? await generator.image(at: time).image }.value }`
requirements.preconditions: A video attachment is being shown in a thumbnail box of a known point size.
requirements.expected_result: The work runs off the main actor at user-initiated priority, so opening a movie never stalls drawing. The requested pixel size is the point size doubled and rounded up, used as a square maximum size, so the generator never decodes a frame larger than the box needs. The track's preferred transform is applied, so a portrait video recorded on a phone is not shown on its side. The frame is taken at 0.5 seconds with a timescale of 600, deliberately not at the start, because a black first frame would otherwise become the thumbnail. Any failure yields no image and the caller keeps its placeholder fill.
side_effects: Decodes one video frame
requirements.persistence: Nothing persisted; the frame is held only by the view.
requirements.windows_path: Platform boundary: a Windows media frame grab (Media Foundation source reader or equivalent). The three observable parts are the 0.5-second offset, the doubled-and-rounded-up square size cap, and applying the rotation metadata. Grabbing at time zero gives a black tile on a large share of real recordings.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a fixture video with a black first frame and a rotation flag, asserting a non-black frame at the right orientation and a size no larger than the cap

requirements.title: Finder icons for non-media attachments are cached by a four-way key and bounded at 64 entries evicted oldest first
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:102-106 `/// Finder icons by extension, cached: one lookup per row per render stalled scrolling.` with `@MainActor enum FileIcons { private static var cache: [String: NSImage] = [:]; private static var order: [String] = [] }`

DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:108-120 `static func icon(for path: String) -> NSImage { let key = iconKey(for: path); if let hit = cache[key] { return hit }; let image = NSWorkspace.shared.icon(forFile: path); cache[key] = image; order.append(key); /* Bounded: icons are small but unbounded kinds are not. */ while order.count > 64, let oldest = order.first { order.removeFirst(); cache.removeValue(forKey: oldest) }; return image }`

DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:122-133 `private static func iconKey(for path: String) -> String { let ext = (path as NSString).pathExtension.lowercased(); if !ext.isEmpty { return ext }; var isDirectory: ObjCBool = false; if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: path, isDirectory: &isDirectory), isDirectory.boolValue { return "folder" }; if let type = try? URL(fileURLWithPath: path).resourceValues(forKeys: [.contentTypeKey]).contentType { return "type:\(type.identifier)" }; return "file" }`
requirements.preconditions: An attachment row needs a file icon.
requirements.action: The icon is requested for a path.
requirements.expected_result: The cache key is derived in four steps, in this order: the path's extension lowercased when it is non-empty; otherwise the literal "folder" when the path exists and is a directory; otherwise the literal "type:" followed by the resolved content type's identifier; otherwise the literal "file". Two files sharing an extension therefore share one icon, which is the point. On a miss the icon is read for that specific path and stored under the key. The cache is bounded at 64 entries and evicts in insertion order, oldest first, in a loop, so several entries over the bound are all evicted in one call. Insertion order is not refreshed on a hit, so this is first-in-first-out, not least-recently-used. The source records why the cache exists: one uncached lookup per row per render stalled scrolling.
side_effects: One system icon lookup per cache miss
requirements.windows_path: The bound of 64 and the first-in-first-out eviction are exact. The key derivation must keep its order: testing the extension first is what makes the cache useful, and the directory test must come before the content-type lookup because a directory has a content type too.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a file with an extension, an extensionless file, a directory and 70 distinct kinds, asserting the keys and the eviction order

Three cases: the composer moved to another thread (close what was open and never open on arrival), first appearance (adopt the runtime without opening unless asked), or the same thread (follow the flag as before).'

requirements.preconditions: The composer's changes popover coordinator already serves one thread's runtime and the composer moves to a different thread.
requirements.action: sync is called with the new runtime.
requirements.expected_result: Three separate writes happen, in this order. First the popover is closed. Second, the OUTGOING runtime's isDiffVisible is set to false when it was true, so returning to the first thread later finds its changes panel closed rather than reopening it. Third, after adopting the new runtime and its open-request counter, the INCOMING runtime's isDiffVisible is set to false when it was true, so arriving at a thread that had the panel open does not open one. The second and third writes are separate observable state changes on two different runtimes, not one. The incoming clear is suppressed while website captures are enabled, so a capture run can arrive with the panel already open; the outgoing clear is not so guarded and always happens. The branch returns immediately and does not fall through to the follow-the-flag path. The first-appearance branch applies the same incoming clear, with the same capture guard.
side_effects: Writes isDiffVisible on two runtimes
Closes the popover
requirements.persistence: isDiffVisible lives on the runtime, not in user defaults.
requirements.windows_path: Both clears must be reproduced. Omitting the outgoing one leaves a thread that reopens its panel when you come back, which is a different product; omitting the incoming one pops a panel on every thread switch. The capture guard is dead code in every normal launch (porting/dead_code.md entry 34: the `!CaptureRun.isEnabled` conjuncts at DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:557 and :563) and the capture subsystem is not ported (ED-001), so under ED-061 the port omits the guard and both clears are unconditional.

requirements.title: The changes popover adopts a new thread's open-request counter rather than treating the difference as a request to open
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:593-594 `/// The thread's `diffOpenRequest` as last seen, so a counter that merely differs between two threads never opens the popover.` with `private var seenOpenRequest = 0`

DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:562 the first-appearance branch's `seenOpenRequest = runtime.diffOpenRequest`

DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:596-603 `/// A tool row or a Review button bumped the request on the thread the coordinator already serves; a bump seen only because the composer moved to another thread is not an opener.` with `func reopen(runtime: ThreadRuntime) { guard runtime === self.runtime else { sync(isVisible: runtime.isDiffVisible, runtime: runtime); return }; guard runtime.diffOpenRequest != seenOpenRequest else { return }; seenOpenRequest = runtime.diffOpenRequest; desiredVisible = true; ... }`
requirements.preconditions: Each thread runtime carries its own monotonically bumped diffOpenRequest counter, and two threads hold different values.
requirements.action: The composer moves between threads, or a tool row or Review button bumps the counter.
requirements.expected_result: Whenever the coordinator adopts a runtime, on a thread switch and on first appearance alike, it copies that runtime's current open-request counter into its own last-seen value. A later reopen call therefore compares against the counter of the thread it is actually serving, and a value that merely differs because the composer moved to another thread is not treated as a request to open. A reopen call naming a runtime the coordinator is not serving does not open anything either: it is redirected into sync, which takes the thread-switch path. Only a bump on the thread already served, that is a value different from the adopted one, opens the panel, and that bump is then adopted in turn so it fires once.

requirements.persistence: diffOpenRequest lives on the runtime; the last-seen value is coordinator state.
requirements.windows_path: A counter compared against a remembered baseline, adopted on every runtime change. Comparing against zero, or against the previous thread's value, makes every thread switch pop the changes panel.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test: two threads with different counters, moving between them with no bump (nothing opens), then bumping on the served thread (opens once), then moving away and back (nothing opens)

source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:253-257, the doc comment line by line: "/// The movie aspect-fitted into `imageBounds`, from the video track's natural size" / "/// (preferred transform applied), by path. The track is loaded with the modern async" / "/// API by the thumbnail's own task (see `prefetchVideoSize`); the panel sizes itself" / "/// before the player exists, so an unloaded track falls back to `imageBounds`.", then :264 "@MainActor private static var videoSizes: [String: CGSize] = [:]"

DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:259-272 `static func prefetchVideoSize(for attachment: Attachment) async { guard attachment.isVideo, videoSizes[attachment.path] == nil else { return }; let asset = AVURLAsset(url: attachment.url); guard let tracks = try? await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .video), let track = tracks.first, let (natural, transform) = try? await track.load(.naturalSize, .preferredTransform) else { return }; var size = natural.applying(transform); size = CGSize(width: abs(size.width), height: abs(size.height)); guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return }; let scale = min(imageBounds.width / size.width, imageBounds.height / size.height); videoSizes[attachment.path] = CGSize(width: floor(size.width * scale), height: floor(size.height * scale)) }`

DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:210-211 its only caller, AttachmentVideoThumbnail's `.task(id: attachment.path) { await AttachmentLargePreview.prefetchVideoSize(for: attachment)`
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/TimelineRows.swift:1305-1306 `} else if attachment.isVideo { AttachmentVideoThumbnail(attachment: attachment, size: size)`, the one place the thumbnail is drawn
requirements.preconditions: A video attachment's thumbnail (AttachmentVideoThumbnail, drawn by AttachmentThumbnail for a video) appears in an attachment strip: the composer draft, a queued follow-up, a prompt editor or a sent message.
requirements.action: The thumbnail's task runs prefetchVideoSize for the attachment.
requirements.expected_result: When the attachment is a video and its path has no cached size, the first video track and its natural size and preferred transform are loaded asynchronously; the transform is applied, both sides are made positive, and the size is aspect-fitted into 480 by 360 with each side floored, then stored under the attachment's path. A path already cached, or a non-video attachment, returns at once with no load. The check comes before the two awaited loads and the store after them, so two runs for one path that overlap both load and each stores its result. No track, a failed load, or a zero width or height stores nothing, so the next run of the thumbnail's task tries again. The cache is keyed by path only, has no bound and no eviction, and lives for the life of the process, so a different file later placed at the same path keeps the first size.
side_effects: Reads the video file's track metadata whenever its path has no cached size when a run starts: runs that do not overlap read it once per path while it succeeds, but two runs for the same path whose loads overlap (for example the same file in the draft strip and in a sent message's strip) both read it, because the cache is checked before the awaited loads (:269) and written only after them (:278)
Grows an unbounded, process-lifetime path-to-size map
requirements.persistence: Nothing on disk; an in-memory map for the life of the process.
failure_cases: No readable video track, a failed load or a zero size: nothing is cached and a later run retries.
The thumbnail never appears: nothing is cached and the preview opens at 480 by 360 (PR-COMPOSER-210).
requirements.cancellation: Runs inside the thumbnail's .task(id: attachment.path), which SwiftUI cancels when the thumbnail goes away or its path changes; the source adds no cancellation handling of its own.
requirements.windows_path: An asynchronous media-metadata read of the first video stream's frame size and rotation, the rotation applied, sides made positive, fitted into 480 by 360 with floor, and stored in a process-lifetime dictionary keyed by path with no eviction. Start it from the video thumbnail's appearance, before the thumbnail's frame grab, as the source does; not from the preview's open.
requirements.verification_method: unit test of the fit over a landscape track, a portrait track rotated by its transform and a zero-size track, plus an integration test asserting one metadata read per path across two appearances that do not overlap, two reads for two appearances whose loads overlap, and a retry after a failed read

requirements.preconditions: A merge attempt failed.
requirements.expected_result: At most six attempts. A zero exit returns at once. Otherwise the failure message is kept and the combined stdout plus stderr is lowercased and tested for the substrings "405", "not allowed" and "checking"; retry happens only when the forge is GitLab and at least one matches, otherwise the loop breaks immediately. The backoff between attempts is 3 + attempt * 2 seconds, so 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and then a sixth sleep of 13 seconds that is burned before the loop ends and the error is thrown. requirements.action: The path fails the root test.
requirements.expected_result: changed is set to true FIRST, unconditionally, for every path that gets this far. The root test then requires both that the path begins with the root plus a separator and that its UTF-8 length is strictly greater than that prefix's UTF-8 length. Failing either, everything is set to true and the path is skipped. Two distinct inputs take this branch: a path that is not under the working root at all - which happens when the git directory is a second stream root and something inside it was neither a cookie nor under gitPrefix - and the working root itself, which is exactly the prefix length. The length test is in BYTES against a byte count, while the cookie rule's drop is in CHARACTERS; the two units are not interchangeable and a non-ASCII project path makes them differ.

requirements.preconditions: HydraLaunch.runsNatively is true, so the lead's provider is Claude, Codex or Copilot and the heads stay on it.
requirements.action: The Hydra half of the appended system prompt is built for the lead.
requirements.expected_result:
The body is exactly, with {howToSpawn}, {howToWait}, {briefRule}, {verificationRule}, {projectRule}, {reviewRule}, {autoMergeRule} and {reportStyleRule} substituted:

# Hydra

The user switched on Hydra for this chat: you lead a team of helper agents, called heads, that work in parallel in your checkout. Switching Hydra on is the user asking you to use them, so it overrides any standing rule that says not to spawn agents unless asked. {howToSpawn} The agents you spawn this way are the Hydra heads themselves: Marrow shows each one in the team's panel under a roster name and posts its outcome in the chat. There is no other launcher and no other kind of head, so never tell the user that Hydra heads cannot be started here; when the user asks for heads, spawn them this way.

Delegate first, work second. Anything bigger than a single obvious change to a single file is a job for heads: audits, reviews, a feature that spans files, a refactor, "check everything", research across many files or sources, several tasks in one message. In your first reply, look at the code only long enough to write good briefs, a minute and a handful of files rather than ten, then send out scouts for the reading and workers for the changes, all in that same message. Never spend minutes reading before you delegate, and never do inline what heads could be doing in parallel. Only a truly single-focus request, one file and one obvious change, is yours to do alone, and size the team to the work rather than to how many heads are free: a handful of independent pieces is a team, where three tiny steps that depend on each other are one head's task, or your own.

When you delegate:
- {howToWait}
- Give each head one self-contained task with the exact files, symbols and acceptance criteria it needs. Heads share the checkout but not your context, so write the task as if to a capable colleague who has read nothing yet.
- {briefRule}
- {verificationRule}
- {projectRule}
- Split the work so no two heads edit the same file and no head's task rests on another head's unfinished changes: they run in parallel and never see each other's work. Keep integration, verification and the final answer for yourself: never send out a head to verify, redo or finish another head's work.
- Tell the user in one line which heads you sent out and what each one does. Marrow names the heads in roster order (Hank, Walter, Ada, Otto, Nova, Remy, Iris, Milo, Juno, Ezra, Lena, Bo, Kai, Vera, Finn, Mira, Odin, Suki, Rex, Zola, Pip, Ivo, Lux, Tova, Gus, then Hank 2 and so on): announce each head by its task and use exactly those names in that order, never invented ones. There is no head called Ives; the roster has Ivo.
- After delegating, yield until reports arrive.
- Heads go out through the tools above, never through a fenced hydra block: that is the delegation format for providers without agent tools of their own. If you end a reply with one anyway, Marrow still sends those heads out as threads of their own, but your turn ends there and their reports come back as a later message.

When they report back:
- The checkout changes under you while heads work, and the user may be editing too. Never use git status or git diff to check on a head, and never reconcile, revert, stash or move changes you did not make.
- Take a report as done work: read the files it names if something matters, but do not redo the task and do not start it over because the tree looks different from what you expected. A head that failed leaves its part to you: do it or send it out again. A head the user stopped leaves its part alone unless the user asks.
- Then finish the job: integrate, run one verification if it matters, and answer the user. {reportStyleRule}

With reviewsHeads true, one extra bullet "- " + reviewRule + newline is inserted immediately before the "Then finish the job" bullet. With autoMerges true, a newline, autoMergeRule and a newline are appended after that bullet. With autoMerges false the interpolation contributes nothing but the literal still ends with a newline after the last bullet.
side_effects: The text is joined with AntiSlopPolicy.instructions and passed to the provider: Claude as one --append-system-prompt argument, Codex as params["developerInstructions"], Copilot as params["systemMessage"] with mode "append"
failure_cases: The provider falls outside the three native cases: howToSpawn is the empty string and howToWait is the bare default. Unreachable in the shipped flow (recorded dead in dead_code.md item 18); keep an equivalent unreachable fallback and build no behavior on it.

requirements.verification_method: contract fixture comparing byte for byte across the four flag combinations

requirements.preconditions: A capture of a checkout is stored or under way when a head's work lands in that checkout.
requirements.action: applyHydraHead invalidates the checkout; heads then ask for captures.

Data(contentsOf: url) else { return false }; let body = Data([0x0A]) + data; return body.range(of: opening) != nil && body.range(of: closing) != nil } }.value }
requirements.preconditions: A list of checkout-relative paths.
requirements.expected_result: The scan runs off the main actor at utility priority. For each path: read the file size; skip (not conflicted) when the size cannot be read, when size > 4000000, or when the bytes cannot be read. Otherwise prepend one 0x0A byte to the content and require BOTH the byte sequence "\n<<<<<<< " (note the trailing space) AND "\n>>>>>>> " (trailing space) to occur. The prepended newline lets a marker on the very first line match. Order of the returned list follows the input order.
side_effects: File reads
failure_cases: A deleted file (a deletion the team made) reads as not conflicted.
A file over 4,000,000 bytes is never checked, so markers in a very large file can reach the remote. This is upstream behavior.

requirements.preconditions: Conflict gate passed.
requirements.expected_result: The stage runs as a loop of at most three tries (PR-HYDRAMERGE-127). Each try reads HEAD's commit hash as `head` and advances the stage to "Writing the commit" with step .committing (raw 1). The parent is `head`, except that when the commit goes to the chat's own branch (ownBranch, PR-HYDRAMERGE-038), `git fetch --quiet origin` succeeds, origin/<target> resolves to a commit other than `head`, and `head` is an ancestor of it, the tree is built on that remote commit instead (PR-HYDRAMERGE-128): the parent becomes the remote commit and the three-way-merged contents are kept for the sync (PR-HYDRAMERGE-131). Otherwise a tree is written from a scratch index seeded with HEAD and updated with `git add -A` restricted to the team's paths. Then the lead's readiness is checked again: not ready returns .deferred with no record and no note (PR-HYDRAMERGE-116). Then, if the tree hash equals the parent's tree hash, the pass returns .alreadyOnMain: everything the team did is committed already and this pass posts nothing itself. The caller still marks the work spent, and when every group came back .alreadyOnMain with no strays it runs the settlement of PR-HYDRAMERGE-113. Sibling claims are not checked again after the capture.
side_effects: git rev-parse; on an own branch git fetch --quiet origin, rev-parse --verify origin/<target> and merge-base --is-ancestor; then read-tree, add and write-tree against a scratch index file, or the rebuild of PR-HYDRAMERGE-128; the real index is untouched
failure_cases: A throw from commitHash, captureTree or treeHash falls into the generic catch of PR-HYDRAMERGE-066.
A failed fetch, an origin/<target> that does not resolve, a remote equal to HEAD, or a HEAD that is not its ancestor all fall back silently to the capture on HEAD.
requirements.windows_path: Scratch index file in a Windows temp path; GIT_INDEX_FILE works the same. NUL-separated pathspec stdin is portable. The same fetch, resolve and ancestor gate before rebuilding on the remote.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture on the argv, plus integration tests for the alreadyOnMain case, for a lead that resumes before the readiness check (deferred, nothing sent), and for an own branch whose remote moved ahead
requirements.b2_change: B1 AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:212-218 went straight from `captureTree(paths: sorted)` to `guard try await tree != git.treeHash(of: "HEAD") else { return .alreadyOnMain }`. B2 inserts the readiness guard and the fresh blocking-claims check at :247-259 between them (HEAD comparison now at :263).

requirements.title: hydraBranchName slugs the chat title and appends the first six characters of the chat's own id
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:871-882 - /// The chat's own branch: the same on every try, so a retry after a failed merge /// updates the request it opened. ... private static func hydraBranchName(for lead: ChatThread) -> String { let title = lead.title == ChatThread.untitled ? "team" : lead.title; var slug = title.lowercased().map { $0.isLetter || $0.isNumber ? String($0) : "-" }.joined(); while slug.contains("--") { slug = slug.replacingOccurrences(of: "--", with: "-") }; slug = slug.trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet(charactersIn: "-")); if slug.count > 40 { slug = String(slug.prefix(40)).trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet(charactersIn: "-")) }; let suffix = String(lead.id.uuidString.lowercased().prefix(6)); return "hydra/\(slug.isEmpty ? "team" : slug)-\(suffix)" }
requirements.preconditions: ownBranch is true.
requirements.expected_result: Start from the title, or "team" when untitled. Lowercase it; replace every character that is not a Unicode letter or number with "-"; collapse every run of "--" repeatedly until none remain; trim leading and trailing "-"; if longer than 40 characters take the first 40 and trim "-" again. A slug that is then empty becomes "team". The suffix is the first six characters of the lead chat's own id (lead.id.uuidString) lowercased; uuidString is hyphen-grouped 8-4-4-4-12, so the first six are always hex. The name is therefore the same on every try for the same chat and title, so a retry updates the merge request it opened instead of opening another. The result is exactly "hydra/<slug>-<suffix>".

requirements.preconditions: autoMergeHydraWork(of:) passes its pre-guard (PR-HYDRAMERGE-010) while another chat's merge is running (isAnyHydraMergeRunning).
requirements.expected_result: The runtime's isHydraMergeQueued becomes true. The job then sleeps 400 milliseconds at a time for as long as any live runtime is merging, checking after each sleep whether its task was cancelled and returning at once if so. However the wait ends (the other merge finished, or cancellation), isHydraMergeQueued goes back to false. A job whose runtime is already queued is turned away by the pre-guard, so one chat waits at most once at a time. After the wait every precondition is read again (PR-HYDRAMERGE-010); the first waiter to find no merge running sets isHydraMerging without suspending, so the other waiters see it at their next poll and keep waiting.
side_effects: isHydraMergeQueued is observed state on the lead's thread runtime while it waits
requirements.persistence: none: isHydraMergeQueued defaults to false, is not saved with the thread, and is not among the conditions holdsOnlyPersistedState checks
failure_cases: A waiting job whose lead is no longer ready, or whose setting or Hydra switch went off, when the other merge ends returns silently at the second guard.
Cancelling the waiting task returns with no record and no note.
requirements.cancellation: Cancellable while waiting: the loop checks Task.isCancelled after each 400 ms sleep and returns, clearing the queued flag.
requirements.windows_path: Same flag, the same 400 ms poll on the UI thread, the flag cleared on every exit from the wait, and the re-read of every guard before the merge flag is set with no await in between.
requirements.verification_method: unit test with a fake clock: lead B finishes while lead A merges; assert B is queued, polls, and starts within one poll of A's end without a sweep; a second trigger for B while queued returns at once; cancelling B's wait clears the flag

requirements.preconditions: A project pass reports a failure: no remote, conflict markers, a remote that changed the same lines, a checkout that kept moving, a merge request that could not be opened or merged, or the generic catch.
requirements.action: fail(headline, body, label:, url:, retryable:) runs.
requirements.expected_result: detail is title(headline) + ": " + body, where title() prefixes "<project name>: " when several projects merge. When retryable is true the one-minute retry is scheduled first (PR-HYDRAMERGE-126), whatever happens next. Then, when the lead's last HydraMergeRecord has outcome .failed and exactly that detail, fail() returns .failed with no record and no note. Otherwise it decides from the records already there whether to speak: it speaks when retryable is false, or when the two most recent records are both .failed with retryable true. It appends HydraMergeRecord(at: now, outcome: .failed, project: project name, label:, url:, files: 0, detail:, retryable: true when retryable, else nil), and when it speaks posts a note with title(headline) as its title and body as its body. It returns .failed. So a failure that needs the user is said at once and once; a failure that clears by itself is recorded quietly and said only when it follows two recorded retryable failures in a row, and an identical repeat of any failure adds nothing.

requirements.title: Launch prologue runs six steps in a fixed, load-bearing order before any window exists
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/DroppyCodeApp.swift:3-19 @main struct DroppyCodeApp.init() - the whole prologue, in order: DCInstallNotificationGuard(), signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN), WebsiteCaptures.prepare(), LegacyMigration.run(), HangWatchdog.start(), SwitchLatency.start()
DroppyCode/App/DroppyCodeApp.swift:8-9 comment - 'Before anything posts a notification'
DroppyCode/App/DroppyCodeApp.swift:13 comment - 'Before anything reads settings or the library.'
requirements.preconditions: Process has started; no window, no AppModel and no settings read has happened yet. AppDelegate is attached with @NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor (DroppyCodeApp.swift:5) but applicationDidFinishLaunching has not run.
requirements.action: The process enters the app entry point.
requirements.expected_result: Exactly these six steps run, in this order, synchronously on the main thread, before the scene body is evaluated and before applicationDidFinishLaunching: (1) DCInstallNotificationGuard(), (2) signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN), (3) WebsiteCaptures.prepare(), (4) LegacyMigration.run(), (5) HangWatchdog.start(), (6) SwitchLatency.start(). No other work happens first. The ordering is stated by the source's own comments as load-bearing: the notification guard must precede any posted notification, and the capture prep plus legacy migration must precede any read of settings or the library.
side_effects: Installs a process-wide NSNotificationCenter guard (see PR-LAUNCH-002)
Changes the SIGPIPE disposition process-wide (see PR-LAUNCH-003)
May create capture scratch directories and wipe a defaults suite (see PR-LAUNCH-008)
May copy UserDefaults keys and move an Application Support folder (see PR-LAUNCH-011, PR-LAUNCH-012)
Spawns the hang-watchdog background thread (see PR-LAUNCH-014)
requirements.persistence: Only through the steps it calls; the prologue itself persists nothing.
failure_cases: No step reports failure to the caller; every one of the six is a void call with its own internal try?/guard handling. A failure inside any step cannot abort launch.
requirements.windows_path: A single startup function called before the main window is created and before the settings/library store is first touched, keeping the same relative order for the steps that are ported. Step 1 (an Objective-C exception net) has no Windows analogue and is not ported (port_impacts.md:384 entry 188); step 2 has no Windows analogue (no SIGPIPE) and is replaced by the pipe-write error handling recorded in platform_adaptations PA-0004. Step 3 (WebsiteCaptures.prepare()) is not ported: the capture subsystem is not ported (engineering_decisions.md ED-001, see PR-LAUNCH-008). Step 4 (LegacyMigration.run()) is not ported: BLK-0005 is NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_EVIDENCE under OD-0008 A5 (see PR-LAUNCH-009 to PR-LAUNCH-013). Step 6 (SwitchLatency.start()) is not ported: it is inert outside the development build (engineering_decisions.md ED-005, see PR-LAUNCH-022). Step 5 (HangWatchdog.start()) is the one step ported as a call in the startup function.
requirements.verification_method: unit test on the startup function asserting that HangWatchdog.start() runs in it and that the function returns before the main window is created; restart test asserting no settings or library read occurs before the startup function returns

requirements.title: A process-wide notification guard swallows observer exceptions raised during the two name-based NSNotificationCenter post methods
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/DroppyCodeApp.swift:10 DCInstallNotificationGuard() - the call site, first statement of init()

DroppyCode/App/Window/DCNotificationGuard.m:43-56 DCInstallNotificationGuard - dispatch_once, swizzles postNotificationName:object:userInfo: and postNotificationName:object: with method_setImplementation, each guarded by a NULL Method check
DroppyCode/App/Window/DCNotificationGuard.m:27-41 DCPostWithUserInfoGuarded / DCPostObjectGuarded - @try around the saved original IMP, @catch calls DCNotificationRaised

DroppyCode/App/Window/DCNotificationGuard.m:5-22 DCNotificationLog/DCNotificationOrigin/DCNotificationRaised - os_log_create("iordv.droppycode", "notification"), first MIN(frames.count, 12) callStackSymbols joined by newline
DroppyCode/App/Window/DCNotificationGuard.h:5-19 - doc comment naming the macOS 27 ViewBridge chain and +[NSApplication _crashOnException:]
requirements.preconditions: Process start, before any notification is posted.
requirements.action: An observer raises an NSException while a notification is being posted through one of the two guarded selectors.
requirements.expected_result: The exception does not escape the post. One os_log_error line is written on subsystem "iordv.droppycode", category "notification", with the verbatim format "An observer raised while %{public}@ was posted, dropped: %{public}@ %{public}@\n%{public}@" carrying the notification name, exception.name, exception.reason (empty string when nil) and the first at most 12 call-stack frames joined by newlines. The post returns normally and the remaining work (window ordering, popover presentation) completes. The raising observer still never sees its notification.
side_effects: Process-wide method swizzle affecting every NSNotificationCenter, including Apple framework posts
os_log error entries
failure_cases: If either selector is absent, class_getInstanceMethod returns NULL and that swizzle is skipped silently; the other is still installed.
postNotification: (the NSNotification-object overload) is NOT guarded; an exception raised through it is not caught.
requirements.cancellation: not cancellable; installation is idempotent via dispatch_once, so repeated calls neither stack guards nor lose the original IMPs
requirements.windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY: not ported. port_impacts.md:384 entry 188 - 'DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow and DCNotificationGuard are macOS-only AppKit exception nets: Do not re-implement.' There is no NSNotificationCenter and no ViewBridge on Windows.
requirements.verification_method: no Windows verification; recorded as a macOS-only construct in COMPATIBILITY notes

source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:1304-1314 scheduleSave() - waits max(400 ms, 4 s minus time since lastLibrarySave); when lastLibrarySave is nil, sinceLast reads as a 60 s fallback, and 4 s - 60 s always loses to the 400 ms floor in that max, so the wait is 400 ms, never up to 60 s; a mutation while a save is pending changes nothing
DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:130-137 init() - the running-to-interrupted and running-head-to-stopped repairs exist precisely because a previous run may not have terminated cleanly
DroppyCode/Core/Support/HangWatchdog.swift:5-7 - 'A freeze that ends in a force quit leaves nothing behind'
requirements.preconditions: The process is killed without running applicationWillTerminate.
requirements.expected_result: library.json holds everything written by the last save before the kill. Because a pending save is never restarted by later mutations, a steady stream of changes always gets its first write out within 400 ms and is never starved. Every saveLibrary() call stamps lastLibrarySave, whether it is reached through the scheduled wait or called directly (settle, reopen, thread delete); saveBeforeQuit does NOT call saveLibrary or stamp lastLibrarySave - it writes library.json synchronously by its own separate path. What can be lost is up to about 4 seconds of changes made after the last save; the 60 s value in scheduleSave is only the assumed 'time since the last save' used when there has been none in this run, and it always loses to the 400 ms floor in that max, so the very first save after launch still goes out within 400 ms, not up to 60 s. Thread documents hold whatever their own persistence had written. On relaunch, running turns read as interrupted and running heads read as stopped with a launch-time finishedAt. No recovery prompt, no crash report dialog and no restore-session step is offered.
side_effects: MCP server and terminal children are NOT terminated and may be orphaned, because the termination step never ran
failure_cases: Orphaned child processes after a force kill are upstream behavior and are not cleaned up on the next launch.
requirements.windows_path: Direct port of the recovery behavior. Job Objects with kill-on-close (platform_adaptations PA-0007) would additionally clean up children on a force kill, which is stricter than upstream; that is an improvement to record explicitly rather than assume.
requirements.verification_method: restart test: kill the process and assert the relaunch state
requirements.b3_note: B2's cancel-and-restart 400 ms debounce could starve a steady stream of changes entirely (never quiet long enough to fire) and lost only 'the last 400 ms' when it did fire. B3's scheduler (PR-STORE-015 / PR-LAUNCH-060) always fires the first write 400 ms after the first change of a burst and re-arms at most every 4 s thereafter, so the worst-case loss window is about 4 s of changes, and a steady stream is no longer starved. Review fix (finding #5, MEDIUM): this record's expected_result previously said 'only the direct saveLibrary() calls and saveBeforeQuit stamp lastLibrarySave', and its title/expected_result framed the 60 s scheduleSave fallback as an actual 'up to 60 seconds' loss window. Both were wrong: saveBeforeQuit writes library.json synchronously through its own path and never calls saveLibrary or stamps lastLibrarySave (AppModel.swift:1327-1345); every saveLibrary() call, scheduled or direct, does the stamping (:1318); and the 60 s value is only the assumed 'time since the last save' fed into the max() when there has been none, which always loses to the 400 ms floor, so the wait after a long idle period is still 400 ms, not up to 60 s. Corrected in place; same correction made to E:/Droppy/work/b3/B3_PLAN.md section A32 and the L4b lane packet.

requirements.title: Forwarding aborts on a vanished source, expands and remembers the target project, and discards the new thread when the continuation will not install
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:634 `guard let source = thread(sourceID), project(source.projectID) != nil else { return nil }`
DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:635-636 `let sourceRuntime = runtime(for: sourceID)` then `await sourceRuntime.ensureLoaded()`

DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:637-638 `// The source can be renamed or removed while its history loads.` with `guard let resolved = thread(sourceID), let project = project(resolved.projectID) else { return nil }`
DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:639-643 `let continuation = ThreadContinuation.capture(sourceID: sourceID, title: resolved.title, document: sourceRuntime.snapshotForPersistence())`
DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:647-649 `threads.append(thread)`, `updateProject(project.id) { $0.isExpanded = true }`, `rememberLastProject(project.id)`

DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:650-654 `let newRuntime = runtime(for: thread.id)`, `guard await newRuntime.installContinuation(continuation), self.thread(thread.id) != nil else { return nil }`, `selectedThreadID = thread.id`, `scheduleSave()`, `return thread`
requirements.preconditions: A forward has been asked for on some thread id.
requirements.expected_result: The source thread and its project are checked twice, before and after the source's history is loaded, because the source can be renamed or removed while that load is in flight; either check failing returns nothing and does nothing. The captured continuation carries the source's id, the source's title as it resolved AFTER the load, and a persistence snapshot of the source runtime's document, so the forward carries the conversation as it stands rather than as it was when the menu item was pressed. The new thread is appended to the library, its project is marked expanded, and that project becomes the remembered last project, all BEFORE the continuation is installed. Installing the continuation, or the new thread still existing afterwards, can fail; when either does the call returns nothing and the new thread is neither selected nor saved, so it is left in the library unselected rather than rolled back. On success the new thread is selected and a save is scheduled.
side_effects: Appends a thread to the library
Expands the target project and records it as the last project
Selects the new thread and schedules a library save
requirements.persistence: The new thread, the project's expanded flag and the last-project record, written on the model's save debounce.
requirements.windows_path: The double guard around the await is the load-bearing part: a single check before the load races a delete. The ordering (append, expand, remember, then install) is reproduced as written; the consequence that a failed install leaves an appended unselected thread behind is upstream behaviour and is recorded rather than repaired.
requirements.verification_method: integration test forwarding a thread, forwarding one deleted during its load, and forwarding one whose continuation install fails, asserting the library and selection after each

requirements.title: exportAll rebuilds the proxy routes, writes the provider configs, runs the legacy cleanup and reloads the hub, in that order
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:273-284 exportAll()
requirements.preconditions: Any of: store init, disconnect, setEnabled, a successful probe, saveCustom on a connected server.
requirements.expected_result: servers = enabledServers (computed once). Then, in order: MCPProxy.shared.replaceAll with one route per server that has a non-nil oauthUpstream, each (serverID: server.id, upstream: remote, headers: [:], usesOAuth: true) - every non-OAuth server is filtered out, so the route table holds only OAuth servers and every route carries empty headers and usesOAuth true; MCPProviderConfig.writeAll(servers); MCPExternalSync.sync(servers); and a detached task calling MCPHub.shared.reload(). replaceAll REPLACES the whole table, so a route registered by a probe for a server that is not yet connected is dropped here.

writes or deletes claude.json, codex.json, copilot.json and gemini-settings.json

stops every in-app MCP client process and clears the hub's caches

requirements.expected_result: Before each request (initialize, then each tools/list page) the time left before the probe's deadline is computed; when it is zero or less, exitError(code: nil, ...) is thrown without sending anything. Otherwise the request is sent through MCPStdioConnection.request with that remaining time as its timeout (PR-MCP-235), and the reply carrying the request's id is awaited (PR-MCP-232, PR-MCP-233). When the reply arrives, checkReply runs and the reply is returned. When the connection reports the child's exit (PR-MCP-234), exitError(code: <the exit status>, ...) is thrown. When the timer wins, exitError(code: nil, ...) is thrown. exitError always receives connection.errorTail, the last 4000 bytes of stderr (PR-MCP-236). requirements.preconditions: A stdio connection exists.
requirements.action: The probe finishes, fails or is cancelled, or a hub client stops.
requirements.expected_result: The stdin write handle is closed on the process's serial write queue, whether or not the child is still running. If the child is not running, nothing else happens. Otherwise the terminate signal (SIGTERM) is sent to the child, and 3 seconds later, on a background queue and not awaited, the child is killed with SIGKILL if it is still running. Both signals go to the child's pid alone, never to its process group, so a grandchild such as the node process npx starts is signalled by neither. The probe and every hub client stop their children this same way.

terminates and possibly kills the child process

requirements.action: Bytes arrive on stdout or stderr.
requirements.expected_result: stdout bytes accumulate; every 0x0A byte ends one line, and a partial line is held until it completes. requirements.preconditions: A 2xx response whose Content-Type contains text/event-stream.
requirements.expected_result: When the POST carried no JSON-RPC id (the notifications/initialized notification), the body is nil at once and the stream is never read. Otherwise the stream is read line by line as it arrives. For each line, trim whitespace; skip it unless it starts with "data:"; take the remainder after those five characters and trim it; parse it as JSON; accept it only when it is an object whose "id", read as an integer (an integer, a finite double truncated toward zero, or a string Int() parses), EQUALS the request's id. The first such value is returned immediately, without waiting for the stream to end, so a server that holds the stream open does not hang the caller. A frame for another id, a notification frame without an id and anything unparseable are skipped. When the stream ends without a match the body is nil.
side_effects: none
failure_cases: nil bubbles up as malformed("empty reply") in the probe or "The server sent something unexpected: empty reply." in the hub; the notification's nil body is ignored by both callers
an error while the stream is read is thrown as it is
requirements.cancellation: reading the stream is a cancellation point
requirements.windows_path: Read the event stream incrementally and return at the first matching frame; do not buffer the whole body. On the notification path do not read the stream, and release the unread response so it does not hold its connection open. Note the installed JavaScript bridge accepts a frame with "result" or "error" instead of an id (PR-MCP-196): the clients differ deliberately.

requirements.preconditions: An issuer string.
requirements.expected_result: base = the issuer trimmed of leading and trailing "/". When the issuer parses and has a path that is neither empty nor "/", two candidates come first: "<origin>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server<path>" then "<origin>/.well-known/openid-configuration<path>". The report reads, per OD-0012 E6: "Disconnected, but Credential Manager did not remove this server’s stored values." Where it is shown is not given by the source or by the ruling (open_question). Secrets live in Windows Credential Manager under the same account strings, one item per "MCP <server> <field>".

requirements.open_question: OD-0012 E6 gives the text of the failed-deletion report ("Disconnected, but Credential Manager did not remove this server’s stored values.") but neither the ruling nor the source says where it is shown or for how long.

DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPOAuth.swift:790-793 formEncode - :791 let unreserved = CharacterSet(charactersIn: "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-._~") | :792 return value.addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: unreserved) ?? value
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPOAuth.swift:795-801 oauthErrorMessage
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPOAuth.swift:803-815 origin
requirements.preconditions: none
requirements.action: Any OAuth HTTP call is made.
requirements.expected_result: All three use timeoutInterval 30. fetchJSON is a GET with Accept: application/json; a non-HTTP response throws network("The server didn't answer properly."); any other thrown error becomes network("") which renders as "The network didn't answer."; a non-2xx status or an unparseable body throws metadataFailed("The server answered <status>."). post sends JSON with Content-Type and Accept application/json and returns the data and response without checking the status. postForm builds the body as name=value pairs in the fields' order joined by "&", where every name and every value is percent-encoded as UTF-8 with only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, "-", ".", "_" and "~" left as they are (so ":", "/", "+", "=", "&" and a space are all escaped), falling back to the raw text when encoding returns nil; it sends that body with Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded and Accept application/json, and likewise returns without checking the status. An unparseable URL in any of them throws network("That address isn't valid."). oauthErrorMessage returns the body's non-empty error_description, else its error, else nil. origin builds "<scheme>://<host>" plus ":<port>" when a port is present, and throws discoveryFailed("That address doesn't look like a URL.") when the scheme or host is missing or empty.

failure_cases: the five literal messages above
requirements.cancellation: each request is a cancellation point

The case of the hexadecimal digits in the escapes is UNRESOLVED (B3_PLAN.md 6.1 E4) until checked on the reference runtime.

requirements.preconditions: A stdio request was made on a running child.
requirements.expected_result: The request takes the connection's next id, starts a wait for that id and a timer of `timeout` seconds side by side, and only then queues the request line for the child's stdin. On any failure the other task is cancelled and the id is abandoned: its wait slot is removed and resumed with CancellationError, so nothing is left waiting. requirements.title: One process-launch gate, shared by every ACP session, spaced 1.5 seconds
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:7-21 - `private actor ACPLaunchGate` with `spacing: TimeInterval`, `nextSlot = Date.distantPast`, and `wait()`: `let now = Date.now; let slot = max(now, nextSlot); nextSlot = slot.addingTimeInterval(spacing); if slot > now { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(slot.timeIntervalSince(now))) }`
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:26 - `private static let launchGate = ACPLaunchGate(spacing: 1.5)`
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:110 - `await Self.launchGate.wait()` in start()
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:3-6 - rationale: an agent keeps a store of its own (OpenCode's is SQLite); several starting at once trip over its lock, "database is locked"
requirements.preconditions: configuration.executable is non-nil, so the guard at :109 has passed.
requirements.action: start() awaits the shared launch gate before spawning the child process.
requirements.expected_result: Spacing is the literal 1.5 seconds. A lone start never waits, because `slot = max(now, nextSlot)` equals now when nextSlot is in the past. A batch of N starts is released one every 1.5 s. The gate is a single static instance shared across every ACPSession of every provider and every thread, so a Cursor start and an OpenCode start issued together are still spaced 1.5 s apart.
side_effects: Delays process spawn by up to (N-1) * 1.5 s for a batch of N.
requirements.persistence: In-memory only: nextSlot lives for the life of the app process.
failure_cases: `try? await Task.sleep` swallows the sleep's error; the wait then returns early and the start proceeds.
requirements.cancellation: The sleep's thrown error is discarded by `try?`, so cancelling the awaiting task does not abort the start at this point.
requirements.windows_path: A single module-level async mutex holding nextSlot, awaited in the Electron main process before child_process.spawn. It must be one instance for the whole app, not per session, per window or per provider.
requirements.verification_method: unit (fake clock: the Nth start releases at (N-1)*1500 ms, a single start at 0 ms)

requirements.cancellation: Cancellation of the awaiting task surfaces as CancellationError from the pending request.
requirements.windows_path: Same. Use a case-insensitive indexOf on the message string; do not switch to a code check.

requirements.preconditions: A turn with text and zero or more attachments.
requirements.expected_result: Element 0 is always {"type": "text", "text": <the turn's text>}, even when the text is empty. Then, in attachment order, one {"type": "image", "mimeType": ..., "data": ...} per attachment that is an image AND whose file could be read. When the image is more than 2000 pixels on its longest side and ImageIO can read and re-encode it, data is the base64 of a JPEG thumbnail at most 2000 pixels on its longest side, with the image's orientation transform applied and lossy compression quality 0.8, and mimeType is "image/jpeg". Otherwise (2000 pixels or less on the longest side, or a file ImageIO cannot read or encode) data is the base64 of the file's own bytes and mimeType is the attachment's own mime type. The base64 carries no data: prefix. Non-image attachments and unreadable files are dropped silently. ACPSession itself does not consult supportsImages; Grok's exclusion is enforced upstream in the composer, so an image reaching ACPSession for Grok would still be sent.

Decodes and re-encodes each image over 2000 pixels on its longest side in memory; the file on disk is not changed.

A downscale that fails at any step sends the original bytes with the original mime type, with no notice.

The image codec is a platform boundary: Windows JPEG bytes will not equal ImageIO's, so verification compares dimensions, mime type and orientation, not bytes.

ACPSession.swift:176-179 is unchanged and reads the returned attachment's mimeType.

source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:287-298 - `guard let modelConfigID else { return }; let original = currentModel; for model in models where model.efforts.isEmpty { await setConfigOption(modelConfigID, value: model.id); currentModel = model.id }; if let original, !Self.sameModel(original, currentModel) { await setConfigOption(modelConfigID, value: original); currentModel = original }`

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:281-286 - rationale: Cursor and OpenCode report the effort scale of the current model only, so each model without a scale is made current in turn and its scale read off the reply; models that arrived with a scale (Grok lists them in _meta.reasoningEfforts) are skipped

Each reply re-enters applyConfigOptions, which writes that model's scale onto it and rebuilds the list while preserving earlier findings. Afterwards the model the session started on is restored, but only when it differs by base id from where the walk ended.

failure_cases: Each setConfigOption swallows its own failure, so a rejected model simply keeps an empty scale.

requirements.title: Inbound ids accept integers, doubles truncated to integers, and strings

A string id is taken as is. A boolean, null, array or object id fails to parse, and the message is then treated as having no id: with a method it becomes a notification, without one it is dropped.

requirements.title: Line framing splits on the line feed byte only
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioFramer.swift:26-34 - `case .lines: guard let newline = buffer[search...].firstIndex(of: 0x0A) else { search = buffer.endIndex; break }; messages.append(Data(buffer[start..<newline])); start = newline + 1; search = start; continue`
requirements.preconditions: Bytes arrived from the child's stdout, framing is .lines.
requirements.expected_result: Messages are split on the byte 0x0A only. The carriage return 0x0D is NOT a separator and stays at the end of the preceding message; it is removed later by the delivery step. A message is the bytes between separators, exclusive. Incomplete trailing bytes stay buffered.

A CRLF-writing Windows CLI therefore yields messages ending in 0x0D, which the delivery step strips (PR-PROVACP-155) - note that port_impacts #18 says the source does not strip CR, which is true of the framer but NOT of StdioProcess.deliver.
