requirements.title: The framer rescans only new bytes and compacts its buffer after each append
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioFramer.swift:19-23,58-60 - `buffer.append(data); var start = buffer.startIndex; var search = start + scanned`; and at the end `scanned = search - start; if start != buffer.startIndex { buffer = Data(buffer[start...]) }`
requirements.preconditions: A partial message is buffered and more bytes arrive.
requirements.expected_result: The scan resumes at the offset already searched rather than from the start, so a large partial message is not rescanned on every chunk. After extracting whatever it can, the framer keeps only the unconsumed remainder and records how much of it has been searched. Correctness requirement: a message split across any number of chunks is delivered exactly once and intact.
requirements.windows_path: Same incremental behavior is required, not just the same result: an agent streaming a multi-megabyte tool output in small chunks must not cost quadratic time.
requirements.verification_method: unit (byte-at-a-time feed of a 1 MB message) plus a performance guard

requirements.title: Content-Length framing reads a header block terminated by a blank line, then exactly that many bytes
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioFramer.swift:13,35-54 - separator is the four bytes of "\r\n\r\n"; when bodyLength is nil the framer looks for that separator, parses the header, and on a nil length continues without consuming a body; when a length is known and enough bytes are buffered it emits exactly `length` bytes and clears bodyLength
requirements.preconditions: framing is .contentLength.
requirements.expected_result: The header block ends at the literal four-byte sequence CR LF CR LF. A header block whose Content-Length cannot be parsed, and equally a header block that has no Content-Length line at all, is skipped and scanning continues after the separator without consuming any body; because no body is consumed, the bytes that were meant as that message's body become the start of the next header block. Once a length is known, the body is exactly that many bytes and any surplus stays buffered for the next message. When the separator is not yet present the search pointer is set to max(start, endIndex minus three), that is endIndex minus three but never before the start of the unconsumed data, so a separator straddling two chunks is still found.
failure_cases: A malformed header, or a header block with no Content-Length line, silently discards that header and resumes scanning; the intended body bytes are then scanned as the next header block.
requirements.windows_path: Same. ACP never uses this mode - ACPSession takes the .lines default - but the framer is shared with the Copilot connection, so the mode must exist and behave identically.
requirements.verification_method: unit
requirements.spec_fix: The record said the search pointer is "rewound to endIndex minus three" and covered only a header "whose Content-Length cannot be parsed" -> StdioFramer.swift:38 clamps it, `search = max(start, buffer.endIndex - 3)`; StdioFramer.swift:41-44 moves start past the separator before `guard let length = Self.contentLength(in: header) else { continue }`, and contentLength returns nil both for an unparsable value and for a block with no Content-Length line (:71-80), so either block is skipped with no body consumed and the bytes meant as the body are scanned as the next header block.

requirements.title: Content-Length header parsing is case-insensitive and rejects negative lengths
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioFramer.swift:71-80 - `for line in header.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) { let parts = line.split(separator: ":", maxSplits: 1); guard parts.count == 2, parts[0].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).lowercased() == "content-length" else { continue }; guard let length = Int(parts[1].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)), length >= 0 else { return nil }; return length }` and, after the loop, `return nil`
requirements.preconditions: A header block was found.
requirements.expected_result: Each header line is split once, on the first colon Character after any colons that open the line: Swift split(separator: ":", maxSplits: 1) keeps its default omittingEmptySubsequences, so leading empty pieces are dropped and do not use up the one split (":Content-Length: 1" and "::Content-Length: 1" match), and because the separator is a Character, a colon that forms one grapheme with a following combining mark or ZWJ, or with a preceding Prepend scalar, does not split. A line must yield two parts: "Content-Length:" with nothing after the colon yields one part, so that line is skipped and later lines are still read, while "Content-Length: " (whitespace only after the colon) yields two parts and returns nil for the whole block. Header names are compared case-insensitively after trimming Foundation .whitespaces (tab, every Zs character and U+200B), so "content-length", "Content-Length" and "CONTENT-LENGTH" all match. The value is trimmed of the same set and must parse with Swift Int() to a value of zero or more: Int() accepts a leading '+', "-0" (which is 0) and leading zeros, and rejects anything above Int64.max. A negative, non-numeric, empty or out-of-range value returns nil for the WHOLE header block, not just that line. The first line whose name matches decides the result; later lines are not read. The header is split into lines on every Character.isNewline, which covers LF, VT, FF, CR, CR LF, NEL (U+0085), U+2028 and U+2029. When no Content-Length line is present the result is nil. A zero length is valid and produces an empty message.
requirements.windows_path: Same.
requirements.verification_method: unit (header table)
requirements.spec_fix: The record (its source_evidence summary and expected_result) said the parser "splits each line on the first colon", "requires two parts" without the consequence, trims "spaces", accepts "an integer of zero or more" and splits the header "on newlines" -> StdioFramer.swift:72-76: `header.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline)` splits on every Character.isNewline (LF, VT, FF, CR, CR LF, NEL, U+2028, U+2029); `line.split(separator: ":", maxSplits: 1)` omits empty leading pieces and matches only a standalone colon Character; `parts.count == 2` skips "Content-Length:" but not "Content-Length: ", which reaches `Int(...)` with an empty string and returns nil for the block; `.whitespaces` is tab, Zs and U+200B; `Int(...)` accepts '+', "-0" and leading zeros and rejects values above Int64.max. source_evidence now quotes :72-79 instead of the summary.

requirements.title: finish() releases a trailing unterminated line, but only in line framing
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioFramer.swift:63-69 - `let remainder = framing == .lines && !buffer.isEmpty ? buffer : nil; buffer = Data(); scanned = 0; bodyLength = nil; return remainder`
requirements.preconditions: The child's stdout closed with bytes still buffered.
requirements.expected_result: In line framing a non-empty remainder is returned and delivered, so a final JSON line written without a trailing newline is still processed. In Content-Length framing the remainder is DISCARDED, because a partial body is not a message. All framer state is reset either way, so the framer is reusable.
requirements.windows_path: Same asymmetry.
requirements.verification_method: unit

requirements.title: Outbound frames are newline-terminated in line framing and header-prefixed in Content-Length framing
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:90-104 - `let body = message.data(); switch framing { case .lines: payload = body + Data([0x0A]); case .contentLength: payload = Data("Content-Length: \(body.count)\r\n\r\n".utf8) + body }; try? handle.write(contentsOf: payload)`; JSONValue.swift:59-63 - `data()` serializes with `.fragmentsAllowed` and `.withoutEscapingSlashes`, falling back to the four bytes of `null`
requirements.preconditions: A frame is being written.
requirements.action: send() runs on the write queue.
requirements.expected_result: In line framing the JSON body is followed by a single 0x0A, never CRLF. The body is compact JSON with NO pretty printing, NO sorted keys and, importantly, forward slashes NOT escaped, so a URL inside a prompt goes out as https://example.com rather than https:\/\/example.com. A serialization failure writes the literal `null`. Write failures are swallowed.

requirements.windows_path: Same: terminate with 0x0A only, and do not let the platform translate it to CRLF - write raw bytes to the stdin stream, not through a text-mode writer. Do not escape forward slashes.

requirements.title: Each framed message has trailing carriage returns and spaces removed, and is dropped when empty or unparseable
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:147-152 - `while let last = line.last, last == 0x0D || last == 0x20 { line.removeLast() }; guard !line.isEmpty, let message = JSONValue.parse(line) else { return }; continuation.yield(message)`
requirements.preconditions: The framer produced a message.
requirements.expected_result: Trailing bytes are stripped one at a time while they are the carriage return 0x0D or the space 0x20 - so a CRLF-terminated line and a space-padded line both parse. Tabs are not stripped. An empty result is dropped. A body that does not parse as JSON is dropped SILENTLY: a CLI that prints a banner or a progress line to stdout is ignored rather than breaking the session. Parsing uses fragmentsAllowed, so a bare JSON scalar is accepted and then discarded by handle()'s object check.
side_effects: A parsed message is yielded to the connection's reader.
failure_cases: Non-JSON stdout noise disappears with no log and no notice.
requirements.windows_path: Same two-byte strip. This is what makes a CRLF-writing Windows CLI work despite the LF-only framer.
requirements.verification_method: unit (CRLF line, padded line, banner line)

requirements.title: The stderr tail keeps at most the last four kilobytes for display and trims its buffer at sixty-four kilobytes
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:51-53 - `var errorTail: String { state.withLock { String(decoding: $0.errorBuffer.suffix(4_000), as: UTF8.self) } }`

DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:159-166 - `state.withLock { state in state.errorBuffer.append(data); if state.errorBuffer.count > 64_000 { state.errorBuffer = Data(state.errorBuffer.suffix(16_000)) } }`
requirements.preconditions: The child writes to stderr.
requirements.action: Bytes are appended and later read.
requirements.expected_result: The buffer grows until it exceeds 64,000 bytes, at which point it is cut to its last 16,000 bytes. errorTail decodes the last 4,000 bytes as UTF-8, so a multi-byte character straddling that boundary is replaced rather than dropping the read. These three literals are the contract: 64,000, 16,000 and 4,000.

requirements.windows_path: Same three limits, measured in bytes not characters.
requirements.verification_method: unit (feed 100 KB, assert the trim points)

requirements.title: Terminating closes stdin first, then asks the process to stop, then kills it three seconds later
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:120-129 - `let handle = stdin.fileHandleForWriting; writeQueue.async { try? handle.close() }; guard process.isRunning else { return }; process.terminate(); let process = process; DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 3) { if process.isRunning { kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL) } }`
requirements.preconditions: stop() was called, or the connection was closed.
requirements.expected_result: Stdin is closed on the write queue, so it is ordered after any frames already queued. A process that is not running returns at that point, with no signal. Otherwise SIGTERM is sent and, exactly 3 seconds later and only if the process is still running, SIGKILL is sent to THAT PROCESS ONLY - the pid, not the process group, so grandchildren are not killed.
side_effects: The child is terminated. Any grandchildren it spawned, such as an mcp-remote npx process, are left running.
failure_cases: A child that ignores SIGTERM runs for a further 3 seconds.
requirements.windows_path: Named platform boundary. Windows has no SIGTERM with delivery semantics: per port_impacts #24, TerminateProcess is the practical equivalent and behaves like SIGKILL, so the graceful window collapses. The specification for Windows is: close stdin first, then request termination, then after the same 3 seconds force-kill if still running - preserving the ordering and the 3-second timing even though the first step is already forceful. Do NOT introduce a Job Object group kill here: the source kills the pid only, and killing the group would change observable behavior for mcp-remote grandchildren. PA-0007's Job Object candidate applies to Shell.swift, which is a different code path.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test on Windows (assert stdin closes first, the child dies, and a grandchild survives, matching macOS)

requirements.title: Stdout closing finishes the message stream, after flushing any buffered remainder

requirements.preconditions: The child closed stdout or exited.
requirements.expected_result: Any trailing unterminated line is delivered as a message first (line framing only), then the AsyncStream finishes, which ends the connection's reader loop and triggers didClose. So a final reply written without a newline is still processed before the connection is declared closed.
side_effects: Ends the message stream; leads to JSONRPCConnection.didClose.
requirements.windows_path: Same ordering: flush the remainder, then end the stream.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture (final frame with no trailing newline)
requirements.b2_change: Re-cited only, behaviour unchanged: finishOutput moved from B1 StdioProcess.swift:150-153 (`lock.withLock({ framer.finish() })`) to B2 :153-156 (`state.withLock({ $0.framer.finish() })`).

requirements.title: Process exit waits one second before forcing the output stream closed, because a grandchild can hold stdout open
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:168-183 - `didExit` sets `state.exitStatus = status` and takes and clears `state.exitWaiters` inside `state.withLock`, resumes every waiter with the status, then `DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 1) { [weak self] in handle.readabilityHandler = nil; self?.finishOutput() }`; comment at :177: a grandchild can inherit stdout and keep it open after the provider exits
requirements.preconditions: The child process exited.
requirements.expected_result: Exit waiters are resumed immediately with the exit status. One second later the stdout readability handler is removed and finishOutput is forced, so a grandchild holding the pipe open cannot keep the session alive indefinitely. The delay is the literal 1 second, and it means a crashed agent's exit is reported to the chat about a second after the process died. finishOutput is idempotent in effect because continuation.finish() on an already-finished stream is a no-op.
side_effects: Delays the .exited event by about one second after a crash.
requirements.windows_path: Same 1-second forced close. It matters more on Windows, where an mcp-remote npx grandchild inheriting the handle is common and there is no process-group cleanup (see PR-PROVACP-157).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test (agent exits while a grandchild holds stdout; assert the exited event within about a second)
requirements.b2_change: Re-cited only, behaviour unchanged: B1 StdioProcess.swift:164-179 (NSLock, `lock.withLock { exitStatus = status ... }`) -> B2 :167-182 (`state.withLock { state in state.exitStatus = status ... }`); the 1 second forced close is the same.

requirements.title: PendingReplies registers a request id before sending, honours cancellation, and can time out to a value or a cancellation error
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/PendingReplies.swift:3-6 - `/// Replies waiting on a request id. The id is registered before `send` runs, so a fast` / `/// reply can't arrive before anyone is waiting for it.` / `@MainActor` / `final class PendingReplies<Value: Sendable> {`

DroppyCode/Core/Support/PendingReplies.swift:9-36 register(_:timeout:timeoutValue:send:) - `try Task.checkCancellation()` (:17); `continuations[id] = continuation` then `send()` (:19-20); with a timeout, `Task { try? await Task.sleep(for: timeout); if let timeoutValue { self.resolve(id, timeoutValue) } else { self.fail(id, CancellationError()) } }` (:21-29); `onCancel: { Task { @MainActor [weak self] in self?.continuations.removeValue(forKey: id)?.resume(throwing: CancellationError()) } }` (:31-35)
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:306 and DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:260-270 - the two users
requirements.preconditions: A caller registers a request id, optionally with a timeout and a timeout value, and a send closure.
requirements.expected_result: If the calling task is already cancelled, register throws CancellationError and neither stores the id nor calls send. Otherwise the waiting continuation is stored under the id first and send runs after it, so a reply that comes back at once always finds its waiter. With a timeout, a separate task that does not inherit the caller's cancellation sleeps for that duration and then resolves the id with timeoutValue when one was given, or fails it with CancellationError when none was; if the id was already answered this does nothing. When the calling task is cancelled while waiting, a main-actor task removes the entry and resumes the waiter by throwing CancellationError; a reply that won the race has already resumed it, and then the removal finds nothing.
side_effects: Calls send exactly once when not already cancelled
Starts one timer task per registration that has a timeout
failure_cases: Already cancelled: CancellationError, send not called
Timeout without timeoutValue: CancellationError
Cancelled while waiting: CancellationError
requirements.cancellation: Cancellation is honoured before the send and while waiting; the timeout task is not cancelled with the caller and runs to the end of its sleep.
requirements.windows_path: A main-thread-confined map from string id to a waiter (for example a TaskCompletionSource) with the same order: cancellation check, store, send, optional timer, and removal plus a cancellation fault on cancel. The Swift CancellationError maps to the port's cancellation error (B3_PLAN.md section 3 N1, Core.Support.PendingReplies).
requirements.verification_method: unit: pre-cancelled (no send, CancellationError); a reply sent synchronously from inside send is received; a timeout with and without timeoutValue; cancellation while waiting; a reply racing a cancellation

An image whose width or height is greater than 2000 pixels is sent as a JPEG re-encoded at lossy quality 0.8, at most 2000 pixels on its longest side, with its orientation transform applied, and its data URL reads data:image/jpeg;base64,<payload>. requirements.title: Codex falls back to forking the thread when the server refuses rollback on a paginated thread
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CodexSession.swift:213-215 - catch let error as RPCError where error.message.contains("paginated threads do not support thread/rollback") { return try await forkHistory(...) }
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CodexSession.swift:270-303 - forkHistory
requirements.preconditions: thread/rollback failed with that exact substring.
requirements.expected_result: The fallback fires ONLY on an RPCError whose message contains the substring "paginated threads do not support thread/rollback". With no previousID (the target was the first turn) the original thread is archived with "thread/archive", threadID and turnID are cleared and nil is returned. Otherwise the thread parameters plus "threadId" (the original), "lastTurnId" (previousID) and "excludeTurns" = true are sent as "thread/fork"; the result must carry a string thread.id DIFFERENT from the original, else "Codex did not create a conversation at the revert point." is thrown. The new thread's last turn is then verified with a one-element descending thread/turns/list whose first id must equal previousID and must not equal the target, else "Codex did not confirm the reverted conversation history." is thrown. On success the ORIGINAL thread is archived; on any throw inside that verification block the NEW thread is archived instead with try? and the error is rethrown. Finally threadID becomes the new id, turnID is cleared, activeModel is updated from result.model when present, and the new id is returned.
side_effects: Up to four RPC round trips; one thread archived either way
requirements.persistence: The thread's resume id changes to the forked thread's id, or becomes nil when the whole conversation was archived.
failure_cases: The two exact messages above; a failed verification archives the new thread and rethrows.

requirements.preconditions: Provider detection is resolving the Command Code CLI.
requirements.expected_result: The primary name is the bare string "cmd". When a custom path is set it is used instead and no fallback is tried. Otherwise PATH is searched for "cmd"; failing that, the fallback list is searched in order and the FIRST executable file wins: which("command-code"), which("commandcode"), which("cmd"), then, for each of <home>/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, <home>/.npm-global/bin and <home>/.volta/bin, the names "command-code" then "cmd". The comment records why: "cmd" is the documented alias and "command-code" and "commandcode" are the package's own names.
side_effects: Filesystem probes
requirements.persistence: The resolved path is used for every later spawn.
failure_cases: Nothing resolvable leaves configuration.executable nil, which start() reports as not installed.
requirements.windows_path: THIS IS THE NAMED WINDOWS HAZARD. Resolving the bare name "cmd" through PATH plus PATHEXT on Windows finds C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe, the command interpreter, long before any provider CLI; launching it with this provider's argv would open a console that speaks no protocol on stdout and the session would hang at the first read. UNK-0006 is RESOLVED by PA-0016 (ENGINEERING DECISION): resolution honours PATHEXT, and a candidate whose Windows version resource identifies it as the command interpreter (CompanyName Microsoft Corporation with OriginalFilename Cmd.Exe or Cmd.Exe.MUI, or FileDescription Windows Command Processor), or which is %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe or %SystemRoot%\SysWOW64\cmd.exe, is rejected. PA-0016 validates identity before any resolution is accepted, so the fallback which("cmd") is checked too. If nothing else resolves, the provider reports not installed, exactly as the source does when nothing is found, and the user can point the existing binaryPath setting at the executable. The fallback directories are macOS and Unix package-manager paths; where an npm or volta install puts the Command Code CLI on Windows is not in the pinned source and stays a live-verification item under PA-0016, which is unverified against a real Command Code Windows install.
requirements.verification_method: PA-0016's Windows contract test: with no Command Code installed, resolution returns not installed rather than System32\cmd.exe, and a stub executable whose version resource does not identify the command interpreter IS accepted; plus a unit test on the fallback order; plus a live Windows probe recording where the CLI actually installs

requirements.title: Command Code lists models from the CLI's own printed table, keeping one default
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeAPI.swift:179-234 - listModels and parseModels with the doc comment

requirements.expected_result: Shell.run(executable, ["--list-models", "--no-auto-update"], environment:, timeout: 30) runs and its STDOUT is ANSI-stripped. The user's config.json supplies the configured model from "model" and the configured efforts object from "reasoningEffort". Parsing: each line is trimmed; empty lines are skipped; lines beginning with "Available models", "Pass the full id", "cmd ", "Docs:" or "Usage" are skipped. Finally: when a configured model matches a row, every other row's isDefault is cleared and that row is MOVED to index 0; otherwise the first row already marked default becomes the only default and nothing is reordered. source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:136-157 - the handshake sequence: `let state = await request(["type": .string("get_state")])` (:136) and `let commandsResponse = await request(["type": .string("get_commands")])` (:146)

requirements.preconditions: The process started and the reader attached.
requirements.expected_result: There is NO initialize. First a request {"type":"get_state"} is sent. Its payload is read from the reply's "data" when present, else from the reply itself. A non-empty "sessionFile" string becomes the session id; failing that, a non-empty "sessionId" string does. The context window is taken from data.model.contextWindow. .sessionReady is emitted with the session id or the EMPTY STRING. Then a request {"type":"get_commands"} is sent, its payload read the same way, and each entry of "commands" with a string "name" becomes a SlashCommand with that name and its "description" or the empty string; a non-empty list is emitted as .commands. Finally started becomes true and stopped false, and start() returns the session id or the empty string.

requirements.persistence: The session id is the thread's persisted resume id.

Each resolves with JSON null after 30 seconds, at once when pi exits (didClose resolves every waiting request with null first, PR-PROVCLI-299), and at once when start()'s own task is cancelled; a request whose task is already cancelled is not written at all (PR-PROVCLI-276). requirements.cancellation: Cancelling start()'s task makes the waiting handshake request, and any later one, return JSON null at once; a request made after the cancellation is never written to stdin. start() does not throw for it: it carries on and returns the session id or the empty string.

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:57 `private var pendingResponses = PendingReplies<JSONValue>()`, with DroppyCode/Core/Support/PendingReplies.swift:10-36 register (PR-PROVACP-164)
porting/extracts/provider-argv-and-handshakes.md section 6.9
requirements.preconditions: A live process.
requirements.expected_result: With no process the call returns JSON null at once, with no id used. Otherwise requestCounter is incremented BEFORE use, so the first id is exactly "droppy-1"; the literal prefix is "droppy-", NOT "marrow-" as Claude uses (PR-PROVCLI-019, OD-0012 F1). The id is added to the request object. If the calling task is already cancelled, the call returns JSON null without writing the line, and the id number is still used up. Otherwise the id is registered first and the line is then written. The call returns the whole reply message when a line arrives whose type is "response" and whose id matches. It returns JSON NULL when 30 seconds pass first, when the process closes first (didClose resolves every waiting request with null before anything else, PR-PROVCLI-299), or when the calling task is cancelled while waiting. It NEVER THROWS. The consequence, recorded as an upstream oddity: a hung get_state leaves start() returning an EMPTY session id rather than reporting an error, and the thread then believes it has a session it cannot resume.
side_effects: One stdin line per request
failure_cases: A hung CLI silently produces an empty session id and an empty command list.
requirements.cancellation: Bounded by the 30 second timer, by the process closing and by the caller's cancellation, whichever comes first; an already-cancelled caller writes nothing. The 30 second timer is not cancelled with the caller.
requirements.windows_path: None beyond the port's PendingReplies (B3_PLAN.md section 3 N1) with a 30 second timeout whose value is JSON null. The id prefix is a contract with the app's own reader. It is "droppy-", which is neither "Droppy Code" nor "droppy-code", the two spellings OD-0012 F1 renames, so it is kept.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with a stand-in that never answers get_state, asserting start() returns an empty id after 30 seconds; plus a stand-in that exits while a request waits (null at once), a caller cancelled while waiting (null at once) and a pre-cancelled caller (null, no stdin line, requestCounter advanced)

requirements.title: Antigravity classifies a tool by name into one of eight kinds, then builds the row from ordered parameter key lists (dispatch contract)
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:625-665 - makeToolCall with the doc comment at :620-624
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:693-705 - path(in:) and string(in:keys:)
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:707-712 - lineRange
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:714-718 - humanize
requirements.preconditions: A tool name and its parameters.
requirements.expected_result: This requirement fixes the DISPATCH and the shared helpers; each kind has its own requirement. makeToolCall is NON-OPTIONAL: every tool gets a row and none is hidden. It first calls Self.kind(of: name), a switch over seven literal name lists with a .other default, then resolves the relative path ONCE with Self.path(in:) (PR-PROVCLI-421), then switches on the KIND, not on the name. The eight kind branches are .command (PR-PROVCLI-413), .read (414), .edit (415), .search (416), .web (417), .agent (418), .mcp (419) and .other (420). The shared helpers are string(in:keys:) (422), lineRange(in:) (423) and humanize (424). Per the comment at AntigravitySession.swift:620-624 the stream sends a display subset of the parameters and NEVER the edit content, which is why the edit rows carry a path-only FileEdit.
failure_cases: No recognizable key falls back to the humanized tool name.
requirements.windows_path: relativePath has the same prefix-stripping caveat as PR-PROVCLI-062. The en dash must survive as a non-ASCII character. Note Antigravity's humanize uses `capitalized` on the first word, which lowercases the remaining characters of that word, unlike Command Code's humanize which only uppercases the first character - the two must not be shared.
requirements.verification_method: unit test - the seven name lists and their default, and that the row switch is on the kind rather than the name

source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:342-350 - static func codexSkills(_ result: JSONValue) -> [Self] { (result["data"]?.array ?? []).flatMap { entry in (entry["skills"]?.array ?? []).compactMap { skill in ... } } }
requirements.preconditions: A skills/list result came back (PR-PROVCLI-096).

requirements.title: codexInput sends one plain text part unless the command owns a skill and the text still names it
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:325-328 - func codexInput(for text: String) -> [JSONValue] { guard let skillPath, Self.name(in: text) == name else { return [["type": "text", "text": .string(text)]] }

DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:301-304 - static func name(in text: String) -> String? { guard text.first == "/" || text.first == "$" else { return nil }; return text.dropFirst().split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace).first.map(String.init) }
requirements.preconditions: A Codex turn is being built with a command attached (PR-PROVCLI-081).
requirements.expected_result: Two conditions must both hold for the skill shape: the command has a non-nil skillPath, AND SlashCommand.name(in: text) equals this command's name. name(in:) returns nil unless the text starts with "/" or "$", then takes everything up to the first whitespace after that first character. When either condition fails the result is exactly ONE part, {"type":"text","text":<the unmodified text>} - so a command the user has edited away from (for example by rewriting the leading word) degrades to a plain message rather than sending a mismatched skill.
failure_cases: A command with no skillPath, such as a Claude-style command, always takes the plain path.
requirements.windows_path: The text is passed through unmodified on this path, including its leading slash.
requirements.verification_method: unit test - matching text, mismatched text, and a command with no skillPath

requirements.title: A Codex skill turn rewrites the leading slash into a dollar sign
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:330 - ["type": "text", "text": .string("$" + text.dropFirst())]

requirements.expected_result: The first part is {"type":"text","text":<rewritten text>} where the rewritten text is the literal "$" followed by the ORIGINAL text with its first character dropped. String(parts[1]) : "MCP"; let tool = parts.count > 2 ? parts[2...].joined(separator: "__") : name; return ToolCall(kind: .mcp, title: "\(server) · \(tool)", detail: input.isNull ? nil : input.compactString) }

requirements.action: A name not matched by any case above is dispatched and starts with "mcp__".

requirements.persistence: The row is persisted with the timeline.
requirements.windows_path: The rejoin with "__" and the whole-name fallback are both easy to get wrong; a port that uses a plain three-way split loses the tail of long MCP tool names.

requirements.preconditions: A control request (initialize, set_permission_mode, set_model, interrupt, stop_task) is made from a task that is, or becomes, cancelled.
requirements.expected_result: The process and hasClosed checks come first (PR-PROVCLI-019); then controlCounter is advanced and the id is built. If the calling task is already cancelled, control(_:) throws CancellationError before anything is stored or written: no control_request line is sent, and that id number is used up, so the next request's id skips it. Otherwise the id is registered before the line is sent. If the calling task is cancelled while the reply is outstanding, the waiting entry is removed and the caller resumes by throwing CancellationError, and a control_response that arrives later for that id is dropped; a reply delivered before the cancellation takes effect is returned to the caller as usual. No timeout applies: a caller that is neither cancelled nor answered waits until the reply arrives or didClose fails it. This holds for every control() caller, start()'s initialize included.
side_effects: A request cancelled before the send advances controlCounter without writing to stdin
failure_cases: Cancelled before the send: CancellationError, nothing sent, the id skipped
Cancelled while waiting: CancellationError, and the late reply is dropped
requirements.cancellation: Cancellable before the send and while waiting, as described; the removal on cancellation runs as a separate main-actor task.
requirements.windows_path: Use the port's PendingReplies (the C# counterpart of Core/Support/PendingReplies.swift, B3_PLAN.md section 3 N1) keyed by the "marrow-<n>" id (OD-0012 F1): check for cancellation before registering and sending, and on cancellation remove the entry and fail the waiter with the port's cancellation error.

requirements.preconditions: A provider session (Pi, Command Code or Antigravity) is streaming one assistant turn and holds one StreamedTextTracker (Swift: `var stream`) for it.
requirements.action: The session calls the tracker's mutating methods as the turn's stream events arrive: startMessage/appendMessage for message text, startThinking/appendThinking for reasoning text, and endThinking/endMessage/resetThinking/resetForTurn/resetIDs to close or clear state.
requirements.expected_result: startMessage always mints a fresh message id (messageCounter incremented, id built from it), empties messageText and clears streamedText. appendMessage mints an id only when none is current (the first delta of a turn); otherwise it keeps the current id. Every appendMessage call sets streamedText true and appends the delta to messageText, so a later call accumulates onto the existing buffer. startThinking always mints a fresh thinking id and empties thinkingText. appendThinking mints an id only when none is current: resetsText true (the default, Pi's fallback) does so by calling startThinking, which also empties thinkingText; resetsText false (Command Code's fallback) mints the id directly without clearing thinkingText, so text already accumulated survives. Every appendThinking call, on either path, appends the delta to thinkingText. endThinking and endMessage each clear only their own current id, leaving the accumulated text untouched. resetThinking clears both currentThinkingID and thinkingText together (a message_start that interrupts an in-progress reasoning block drops it). resetForTurn clears only streamedText, leaving ids and text alone. resetIDs clears both currentMessageID and currentThinkingID but leaves messageText, thinkingText and streamedText untouched.
side_effects: messageCounter and thinkingCounter are monotonically incremented counters that never reset, so minted ids stay unique across a session's turns
requirements.cancellation: not cancellable (every method is a synchronous, in-memory state mutation with no suspension point).
requirements.windows_path: Ported verbatim as the sealed class StreamedTextTracker in src/Marrow.Services/Providers/SessionSupport.cs (:45-124, unit N7): Func<long,string> delegates for messageID/thinkingID (Swift `(Int) -> String`), long counters for messageCounter/thinkingCounter (Swift Int), and get-only properties for CurrentMessageID/CurrentThinkingID/MessageText/ThinkingText/StreamedText mirroring the Swift private(set) vars. Shared by every session that adopts SessionSupport; Pi, Command Code and Antigravity keep their own inlined copies until their own lanes switch them over (this unit, lane L2b, only adds the shared type).
requirements.verification_method: unit test per method: StartMessage mints a fresh id, clears the buffer and streamedText; AppendMessage mints an id only when none is current and always sets streamedText, keeping the current id and accumulating text on a later call; StartThinking mints a fresh id and clears thinkingText; AppendThinking exercises both resetsText branches (true starts fresh and clears the buffer, false mints an id without clearing it); EndThinking and EndMessage clear only the current id; ResetThinking clears both the current id and the reasoning text; ResetForTurn clears only the streamedText flag; ResetIDs clears both current ids but not the accumulated text

requirements.preconditions: A tool call that edits a file (a provider session's edit/write tool) is about to run, and the session holds one EditSnapshots (Swift: `var edits`) across the call.
requirements.action: capture(_:path:) is called as the tool call starts; finish(_:path:relativeTo:) is called when it completes. discard/removeAll/text are used elsewhere to drop a pending snapshot, clear all of them, or read a snapshot's captured text without finishing it.
requirements.expected_result: capture reads the file's current text and stores it keyed by the call's id; a file that read(_:) returns nil for (missing, over 1 MB, or undecodable as UTF-8) is stored as empty string, so a call that then writes a brand-new file reports a whole-file addition rather than failing to find a before-text. finish removes and returns that stored before-text; if the id has no stored snapshot (never captured, or already finished/discarded) it returns nil and the row's edits list is left as already queued. Otherwise it re-reads the file's current text as after (again empty if unreadable), turns path into a root-relative path (ToolTitles.relativePath), and if before and after are equal by Swift's canonical `!=` comparison it returns a single FileEdit with no diff; otherwise it returns a single FileEdit carrying both before and after text. discard drops a snapshot without producing a FileEdit. removeAll drops every pending snapshot. text returns the id's captured text, or empty string if nothing was captured for it, without removing it.
side_effects: capture and finish/discard mutate the shared `contents` dictionary keyed by call id, so a session must not reuse a call id across two in-flight snapshots
failure_cases: finish for an id with no stored snapshot returns nil rather than throwing or fabricating text
a file that cannot be read (missing, larger than 1 MB, or not valid UTF-8) is treated as empty string on both capture and finish, not as an error
requirements.cancellation: not cancellable (capture/finish each do a single synchronous file read; no suspension point).
requirements.windows_path: Ported as the sealed class EditSnapshots in src/Marrow.Services/Providers/SessionSupport.cs (:16-44, unit N7), backed by a Dictionary<string,string> keyed with SwiftStringComparer.Instance (:18) rather than plain ordinal string keys, matching Swift's canonical Dictionary<String,String> key equality. Read(path) (:36-40) checks FileInfo.Exists/Length instead of Swift's resourceValues(forKeys: [.fileSizeKey]), and decodes with SwiftText.DecodeUtf8OrNil over File.ReadAllBytes instead of Foundation's String(contentsOf:encoding:), matching this port's established UTF-8-decode convention (keeps a literal U+FEFF for a BOM, unlike Encoding.UTF8's reader/writer defaults) rather than a plain File.ReadAllText call. Finish's before/after comparison uses SwiftString.Equal, not C#'s ordinal ==, to match Swift's canonical `!=` (:31).
requirements.verification_method: unit test per behavior: capture+finish with no change returns a single no-diff FileEdit; capture+finish with a change returns the before/after FileEdit; finish for an uncaptured id returns null; finish reports a path relative to the given root; capture of a missing file and of a file over 1 MB both read as empty so a subsequent write shows as a whole-file addition; discard removes a snapshot without finishing it; removeAll clears every snapshot; text returns the captured text or empty string; and a dedicated test pins Swift canonical string equality (precomposed vs. decomposed accented character), not ordinal ==, for the before/after comparison in finish

source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:42 executableName - case .codex returns "codex"

requirements.action: executable(for:) looks the CLI up on PATH.

requirements.title: Command Code executable name is cmd, which collides with the Windows command interpreter
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:54 executableName - case .commandcode returns "cmd"

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:246-259 fallbackExecutables for commandcode - the comment at :247-248 names "cmd" as the documented alias and "command-code" and "commandcode" as the package's own names
E:/Droppy/port/porting/platform_adaptations.md PA-0016 - "Status: DECIDED, with probe evidence from this machine. Resolves UNK-0006"
requirements.preconditions: Provider is not API-key based.
requirements.action: executable(for:) looks the CLI up on PATH under the bare name cmd, then walks the commandcode fallback list.
requirements.expected_result: The bare name searched first is exactly "cmd". The same string is the Binary path placeholder for the Command Code section.
side_effects: A PATH walk plus the fallback candidate walk.
failure_cases: Nothing found: returns nil.
requirements.windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY AND COLLISION, resolved by PA-0016 (DECIDED; resolves UNK-0006). On Windows the bare name cmd resolves to the system command interpreter (C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe on the probed machine), so a lookup without an identity check would make Command Code read as installed on every Windows PC. Per PA-0016: PATH resolution honours PATHEXT; a candidate whose Windows version resource identifies it as the command interpreter (CompanyName Microsoft Corporation with OriginalFilename Cmd.Exe or Cmd.Exe.MUI, or FileDescription Windows Command Processor), or which is %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe or %SystemRoot%\SysWOW64\cmd.exe, is rejected; if the only match is rejected, Command Code reports not installed, as the source does when nothing is found, and the user can set an explicit path through the existing Binary path setting. The rule keys on version-resource identity and those two paths, not on the file extension. UNVERIFIED against a real Command Code Windows install (PA-0016 residual risk).
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture plus an interaction test proving a system cmd.exe is never accepted as Command Code

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:695 `: "Instead of `\(provider.loginCommand)`: a Studio key from \(provider.apiKeySource ?? "the provider dashboard"), stored in your Keychain and handed to the CLI."` - the optional API key row detail embeds the login command inside backticks

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:608 `get: { providerExpansion[provider] ?? configured(provider) },` and :763-766 `.clipped()` `.disabled(!isExpanded)` `.allowsHitTesting(isExpanded)` `.accessibilityHidden(!isExpanded)` - the card holding this row is collapsed, disabled and not hit-testable unless the provider is signed in or its header was clicked during the page's lifetime
requirements.preconditions: Command Code is installed and not signed in. Its section is expanded: the Sign in row appears only when the provider is not signed in (SettingsView.swift:638-641), and with no header click such a section is collapsed, so the user first clicks the section header (UI-PROVREG-045).
requirements.action: The user clicks the Command Code section header to expand it (UI-PROVREG-045), then clicks Login in that section, or reads the API key row detail.
requirements.expected_result: A terminal opens running exactly "cmd login". The API key row detail reads exactly (OD-0012 G2): Instead of `cmd login`: a Studio key from commandcode.ai/studio, stored in your Credential Manager and handed to the CLI.
side_effects: Writes a login script file and opens it.
failure_cases: Script write failure opens nothing, silently.
requirements.windows_path: The command string is kept verbatim including the backticks in the detail text. The launcher must resolve the Command Code CLI rather than the Windows interpreter (see PR-PROVREG-026). Executable identity is validated per PA-0016: PATH resolution honours PATHEXT, and a candidate whose Windows version resource identifies it as the command interpreter (CompanyName Microsoft Corporation with OriginalFilename Cmd.Exe/Cmd.Exe.MUI, or FileDescription Windows Command Processor), or which is %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe or %SystemRoot%\SysWOW64\cmd.exe, is rejected and the provider reports not installed. The command string "cmd login" is not reworded: PR-PROVREG-026 is settled by PA-0016 (cmd stays a valid invocation name, with executable identity validated), and OD-0008 B6 keeps "Run `cmd login` in Terminal" verbatim. OD-0012 G2: the word Keychain in this detail becomes Credential Manager, the store the port uses (PR-PROVREG-088, 239). How a Windows Login button launches the command is PR-PROVREG-233.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test plus capture comparison of the detail string against the OD-0012 G2 wording

source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:441-448 model(_:for:) - `guard let id else { return nil }`; `if let match = Self.match(id, in: models(for: provider)) { return match }`; `guard provider == .opencode, id.hasPrefix("opencode-go/") else { return nil }`; `return Self.match(id, in: models(for: .opencodeGo))`, with the comment that a thread or pin made before Zen and Go split kept .opencode for a Go model

requirements.preconditions: None.
requirements.action: A view asks for a catalog on appear.

For OpenCode Zen and Go the attempt mark follows the same rule, but the probe itself is memoised (PR-PROVREG-246): an unforced ask after an empty, or empty-after-split, result re-enters loadCatalog and receives the stored result without spawning the CLI. requirements.verification_method: interaction test counting probe launches across repeated asks, including an empty opencode probe followed by unforced asks for Zen and Go

requirements.windows_path: Same ordering, including the asymmetry with the CLI path.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture against mock endpoints, asserting the retry asymmetry

requirements.preconditions: A call to updateCLIIfDue(_:force:), from launch (not forced) or from a turn that failed because the CLI is too old (forced).
requirements.expected_result: The checks run in this order, and each failing one returns false with nothing run: the provider must be Claude or Codex (PR-PROVREG-251); the user must have set no binary path for it. If an update for that provider is already running, an unforced call returns false, and a forced call waits, checking every 500 milliseconds, until that update has finished, then continues. Next the stored attempt dates are read; an unforced call whose provider has a stored date less than 12 hours (43,200 seconds) before now returns false; a forced call ignores the date. Only then is the login environment loaded and the executable resolved; when no executable resolves, false is returned and no date is written. Otherwise the update runs as PR-PROVREG-254 describes.
side_effects: Reads the providerCLIUpdateDates entry (PR-PROVREG-255)
Loads the login environment once past the date check
requirements.persistence: Reads providerCLIUpdateDates; writes nothing on any of these early returns.
failure_cases: A custom binary path is set: never updated, whatever force says
No executable found: false, and no date is recorded, so the next call tries again
A forced call arriving while an update runs waits for it and then runs the updater again, even if that update just installed the newest version
requirements.windows_path: The same gates in the same order: provider predicate, custom path, the in-flight set with the 500 ms wait for a forced call, the 12-hour date check, then the login environment and the executable lookup. The capture-run gate (`!CaptureRun.isEnabled`, :498) is not ported: ED-001 drops the CaptureRun indirection and porting/dead_code.md entry 44 records such short circuits as unreachable from the shipped UI.
requirements.verification_method: unit with a fake clock, settings and executable resolver: a provider other than Claude or Codex, a custom binary path, an in-flight update (unforced returns false, forced waits), a date 11 hours old (skipped) and 13 hours old (runs), a forced call with a fresh date (runs), and no executable (false, no date written)

requirements.expected_result: Returns false immediately unless all three hold: turnID is non-nil, the thread's provider passes ProviderRegistry.updatesOwnCLI (true only for Claude and Codex), and ProviderRegistry.needsNewerCLI matches the error text. When all three hold, it appends an .info notice inside the turn - 'This model needs a newer <provider.displayName>. Updating it, then sending your message again.' (see UI-RUNTIME-039) - so the resend's revert takes the notice away with the rest of the failed attempt, starts an un-awaited Task that awaits finishTurn(status:turnID:) and then resendAfterCLIUpdate(turnID, provider:, error:), and returns true. failure_cases: Any provider other than Claude or Codex, a nil turnID, or an error that does not match ProviderRegistry.needsNewerCLI: returns false and does nothing, leaving the caller to post its own notice and finish the turn as before.
requirements.cancellation: Not cancellable directly; the Task it starts is not stored or cancelled by this function.
requirements.windows_path: Direct port: the same three-condition gate (provider updates its own CLI, error text matches the six needs-newer-CLI substrings, turn id present), the same in-turn info notice text, and the same finish-then-resend sequencing.

requirements.preconditions: finishTurnUpdatingCLI has just finished the turn and started this as an un-awaited follow-up.
requirements.expected_result:
Forces the CLI's own updater via app.providers.updateCLIIfDue(provider, force: true), then reads app.providers.installedCLIVersion(provider). If the version cannot be read, or equals a version already resent at for this provider in cliResendVersions, an error notice with no turn is appended: '<error>

Droppy Code could not bring <provider.displayName> up to date. Run `<command>` in Terminal, then send the message again.' (`claude update` or `codex update`; see UI-RUNTIME-040), and the function returns. Otherwise cliResendVersions[provider] is set to the new version (recording that a resend at this version has been tried, so at most one resend per CLI version per runtime), the session is released with stop: true so the next send launches the new binary, and, only when the runtime is idle, the turn and its user entry still exist and the message is not from Hydra, the failed turn's own user message is resent through resend(turnID, text:, attachments:, restoreFiles: false). Any other state (not idle, turn or user entry gone, or a Hydra-authored message) instead appends an error notice with no turn: '<error>

<provider.displayName> is up to date now (<version>). Send the message again.' (see UI-RUNTIME-041). If the resend call itself throws, the notice is: '<provider.displayName> is up to date now (<version>), but the message could not be sent again: <error.localizedDescription> Send it again.' (see UI-RUNTIME-042).
side_effects: Forces a CLI update check (bypassing the normal 12-hour interval)
Releases and re-launches the provider session (stop: true)
Records the resent-at version in cliResendVersions for this runtime
May resend the failed turn's user message as a new turn
requirements.persistence: cliResendVersions is held on the runtime, not persisted to disk.
failure_cases: installedCLIVersion returns nil, or returns the same version already recorded in cliResendVersions for this provider: 'could not bring ... up to date' notice, no resend attempted.
The runtime is not idle, the turn or its userItemID entry no longer exists, or the entry's message is from Hydra: 'is up to date now ... Send the message again.' notice, no resend attempted.

resend(_:text:attachments:restoreFiles:) throws (for example from its own guards, or Codex's 'no Codex turn ID' refusal): 'is up to date now ..., but the message could not be sent again: <error>' notice.
requirements.cancellation: Not cancellable; runs to completion once started by finishTurnUpdatingCLI.
requirements.windows_path: Direct port: force the CLI updater, compare installed version against the per-runtime, per-provider cliResendVersions guard (at most one resend per CLI version per runtime), release-with-stop before resending, and the three exact notice texts for the three failure branches. `claude update` / `codex update` remain the commands named in the first notice; OD-0002 and OD-0012 F1 govern the app name in the notice text.
requirements.verification_method: unit with a stubbed providers registry: (a) update succeeds with a new version and the runtime is idle with the turn intact - resend is called; (b) installedCLIVersion returns the same version twice - the 'could not bring up to date' notice on the second call, no second resend attempt; (c) the runtime is busy when the update finishes - the 'up to date now, send again' notice; (d) resend throws - the 'up to date now, but could not be sent again' notice

requirements.expected_result: A row in the "Threads" card whose left side is the verbatim title "New thread" on one line, truncated at the tail, with the verbatim sentence "Starts a thread in the current project." as its tooltip rather than as a visible second line. Its recorder shows Ctrl+N while the shortcut is at its default or has been re-recorded to a chord, and the words "Record shortcut" once it has been cleared. The shipped chord renders as Ctrl+N; upstream it is ⌘N, stored as key code 45 with modifiers .command. The persisted override key is the raw value "newThread".
requirements.persistence: An override is stored under the key "newThread" inside the "keyboardShortcuts" JSON blob; a chord equal to Ctrl+N removes the override instead of storing it.
failure_cases: A recorded chord that another command already owns is refused with that command's title; see the refusal requirement.
The shortcut is cleared: the recorder reads "Record shortcut" and the command has no key.
requirements.cancellation: Escape with no modifiers held cancels the recording without changing anything.
requirements.windows_path: The command and its title and tooltip carry over verbatim. The chord does NOT: key code 45 is a macOS virtual key code and the modifier bits are AppKit's, so the port defines the equivalent chord over Windows virtual-key codes and its own modifier set. The Command modifier maps to Control on Windows, which is the default the port ships; port_impacts.md:228 entry 110 requires the persisted blob to be re-defined and the defaults re-derived rather than migrated. Chords render in Windows notation (OD-0008 B7): modifiers as Ctrl, Alt and Shift joined with "+" before the key label, with the ED-050 mapping Command->Ctrl, Option->Alt, Shift->Shift, Control->Ctrl; key labels keep upstream's US-position table (OD-0008 B9). This shortcut therefore reads Ctrl+N.
requirements.verification_method: unit test on the shortcut table asserting the title, tooltip, raw value, section and default chord; interaction test recording and resetting the row

DroppyCode/App/AppCommands.swift:57-58 at 1fbf81e6 - `Button("Actual Size") { model.settings.appZoom = 100 }` `.keyboardShortcut("0", modifiers: .command)`, a hard-coded chord equal to this command's default (key code 29 is the 0 position), outside the shortcut store
porting/owner_decisions.md OD-0002 - "Every user-visible occurrence of the product name inside the app becomes a rename point"; the Windows build ships as Marrow
requirements.preconditions: The Shortcuts page is showing.
requirements.action: The user reads or re-records the "Show Droppy Code" row.
requirements.expected_result: A row in the "Window and panels" card whose left side is the title "Show Marrow" (upstream the verbatim "Show Droppy Code"; its product name is the OD-0002 rename point) on one line, truncated at the tail, with the verbatim sentence "Brings the main window to the front." as its tooltip rather than as a visible second line. In Marrow the command ships with no default chord (OD-0012 G6), so its recorder shows the words "Record shortcut" at its default and after it has been cleared, and the recorded chord in Windows notation once one has been recorded; upstream it ships with ⌘0, stored as key code 29 with modifiers .command. The persisted override key is the raw value "showMainWindow". Ctrl+0 is the hard-coded "Actual Size" zoom command added at 1fbf81e6 (AppCommands.swift:57-58). Upstream both answer Command-0 while this command keeps its default; OD-0012 G6 settles that overlap for the default by giving this command none.
requirements.persistence: An override is stored under the key "showMainWindow" inside the "keyboardShortcuts" JSON blob. Because the default is no chord (OD-0012 G6), clearing the shortcut equals the default and removes the override instead of storing it, and any recorded chord is stored (Shortcuts.swift:300-301 `overrides[shortcut.rawValue] = chord == shortcut.defaultChord ? nil : Override(chord: chord)`, with defaultChord optional at :214).
failure_cases: A recorded chord that another command already owns is refused with that command's title; see the refusal requirement.
The shortcut is cleared: the recorder reads "Record shortcut" and the command has no key.

Upstream, while the default is kept, Command-0 is held both by this command and by the hard-coded "Actual Size" zoom command. In Marrow this command has no default chord (OD-0012 G6), so by default Ctrl+0 is Actual Size alone. A user who records Ctrl+0 for this command recreates the overlap; which of the two then fires is not expressed in source and stays UNRESOLVED with the window area (PR-WIN-224, PR-WIN-226); the port must not pick one silently.
requirements.cancellation: Escape with no modifiers held cancels the recording without changing anything.
requirements.windows_path: The command and its tooltip carry over verbatim; the title carries over except for the product name (OD-0002). The chord does NOT: by owner ruling OD-0012 G6 the command ships with no default chord, because Ctrl+0 is Actual Size and the window can no longer hide (OD-0008 C1). A chord the user records is defined over Windows virtual-key codes and the port's own modifier set (key code 29 is a macOS virtual key code and the modifier bits are AppKit's); port_impacts.md:228 entry 110 requires the persisted blob to be re-defined and the defaults re-derived rather than migrated. The title contains the product name, which the approved rename (OD-0002) changes, so it reads "Show Marrow" (OD-0002; OD-0012 F1); every other title is fixed product text. Chords render in Windows notation (OD-0008 B7): modifiers as Ctrl, Alt and Shift joined with "+" before the key label, with the ED-050 mapping Command->Ctrl, Option->Alt, Shift->Shift, Control->Ctrl; key labels keep upstream's US-position table (OD-0008 B9). This shortcut therefore shows "Record shortcut" until one is recorded. The hard-coded zoom command "Actual Size" keeps Ctrl+0 (PR-WIN-224; OD-0012 G6).
requirements.verification_method: unit test on the shortcut table asserting the title "Show Marrow", tooltip, raw value, section and the absence of a default chord (the recorder reads "Record shortcut"); interaction test recording and resetting the row

requirements.title: A recording session swallows every key event, judges a chord the moment its key goes down, and commits 300ms after the last key is released
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:489-490 doc - "One recording, from the click on the control to the popover folding away. A chord is judged the moment its key goes down and can be replaced while anything is held; it saves once every key is up."

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:525-562 begin - closes any running session, resets state, seeds heldModifiers from the currently held modifiers masked to control, option, shift and command, refreshes the caps, marks itself active, installs `NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: [.keyDown, .keyUp, .flagsChanged])` which returns nil for every handled event (so the app never sees them) and the event itself only for other types, and observes NSApplication.didResignActiveNotification to cancel

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:583-594 handleFlagsChanged - updates the held modifiers; a newly added modifier performs an alignment haptic; with no modifiers and no key held it lets go, otherwise it refreshes the caps; it does nothing while finishing

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:596-608 handleKeyDown - ignores auto-repeats; `if keyCode == 53, flags.isEmpty { cancel(); return }`; otherwise records the held key and modifiers and judges the chord
DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:610-619 handleKeyUp - only for the held key; clears it; lets go when no modifiers remain, otherwise refreshes the caps

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:621-633 judge - latches the chord; a refusal sets the rejected verdict, shows the refusal message and performs a generic haptic; otherwise it sets the accepted verdict, clears the message and performs a level-change haptic

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:635-657 letGo - with no latched chord it only refreshes; accepted marks itself finishing, refreshes, then after 300 milliseconds commits the chord and closes, provided the task was not cancelled and the session is still active; rejected drops the latched chord and returns to listening; listening only refreshes

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:569-581 close - cancels the finish task, removes the event monitor and the resign observer, clears the active and finishing flags, and calls the close callback exactly once

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:659-674 refreshCaps - with a latched chord and a verdict, the chord's caps; otherwise the held modifiers as pressed caps, plus the held key's cap when one is down, or a ghost key when not; with no modifiers at all, a single ghost Command cap; the caps are written only when they changed
requirements.preconditions: A recording popover is open.
requirements.action: The user presses and releases a key combination.
requirements.expected_result: Every key down, key up and modifier change is consumed by the session and never reaches the rest of the app. Auto-repeats are ignored. Pressing Escape with no modifiers held cancels the session outright; Escape with a modifier is treated as an ordinary key. Adding a modifier fires an alignment haptic and redraws the caps. Pressing a key judges the chord immediately: accepted fires a level-change haptic and turns the caps green, refused fires a generic haptic, turns them red and shows the refusal message. While anything is still held the chord can be replaced by pressing a different key. When the last key and modifier are released, an accepted chord is committed 300 milliseconds later and the popover closes; a refused chord is discarded and the session returns to listening with the caps back to neutral. Closing removes the monitor and the observer and calls the close callback once. The application losing focus cancels the session.
side_effects: Blocks all key input to the rest of the app while open
Fires haptics
Writes the shortcut store on commit
failure_cases: A refused chord: it is never committed; the message is shown and recording continues.
The app is sent to the background mid-recording: the session cancels and nothing is committed.
requirements.cancellation: Bare Escape, dismissing the popover, the row disappearing, or the app resigning active. The 300ms commit task is cancelled by all of them.
requirements.windows_path: A window-level capture-phase key listener with preventDefault and stopPropagation on every keydown, keyup and modifier change while the popover is open, plus a blur handler that cancels. port_impacts.md:424 entry 208 records that this is one of five separate Escape policies in the family and must be decided on its own: here bare Escape cancels and Escape with a modifier is recordable. The haptics become a no-op shim; do not substitute a sound or an animation.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test covering accept, refuse, replace-while-held, bare Escape, modified Escape, blur, and the 300ms commit delay

requirements.preconditions: A chord has just been judged.

requirements.expected_result: The checks run in exactly this order and the first that fires wins. A chord identical to the shortcut's current one is always allowed, so re-recording the same keys is not a conflict with itself. A bare modifier key gives the verbatim "Add a key to the modifiers." A key that types text or moves the caret, pressed with no modifier other than Shift, gives the verbatim "Add Ctrl or Alt so typing still works." (OD-0008 B7; upstream "Add ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ so typing still works."). A key with no menu equivalent gives the verbatim "Menus cannot use this key." One of the reserved chords gives the verbatim "Windows or Marrow already uses this chord." (OD-0008 B8; upstream "macOS or Droppy Code already uses this chord."). A chord another command already holds gives that command's title followed by the verbatim " already uses this chord.", for example "Command palette already uses this chord." failure_cases: The four hard-coded zoom chords (Ctrl with +, -, 0 and =, upstream Command) are neither reserved nor AppShortcut commands. Recording Ctrl+- or Ctrl+= for a command is accepted with no message and then shares its chord with a zoom command; Ctrl+0 is refused only while a command holds it, and then by the owner check naming that command, not "Actual Size"; in Marrow no command holds it by default, because showMainWindow ships with no default chord (OD-0012 G6), so recording Ctrl+0 is accepted with no message and shares the chord with Actual Size. Which command fires on a shared chord is not expressed in source (UNRESOLVED; PR-WIN-226). Reproduce the absence of a guard; do not add the zoom chords to the reserved list.
requirements.windows_path: Keep the five checks in the same ORDER so the same chord produces the same message. Two messages are reworded by owner ruling: "Add Ctrl or Alt so typing still works." The reserved table is kept as is (B8), with Command read as Ctrl per ED-050, and must stay in sync with the hard-coded thread-jump chords as one unit (port_impacts.md:228 entry 110).

requirements.preconditions: A provider section is rendering.
requirements.action: The section appears, or a check signs the provider in.
requirements.expected_result: The usage block is present only when the provider exposes plan limits or credits AND its status says it is installed AND its authentication state is not signed-out. The block is a divider, then the plan-limits view when limits are exposed and the credits view when credits are, 14 points apart, inset 16 horizontally and 12 vertically. Becoming visible triggers one refresh of plan limits and one of credits; the observer runs with initial true, so it fires once when the page opens on a signed-in account and again when a check signs one in. requirements.title: Editing an API key debounces 600ms, then re-checks the provider and force-reloads its catalog
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:784-795 - `.onChange(of: apiKey) { _, value in guard provider.acceptsAPIKey, value != model.settings.apiKeyInput(for: provider) else { return }; model.settings.setAPIKeyInput(value, for: provider); keyCheck?.cancel(); keyCheck = Task { try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(600)); guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }; await model.providers.refresh(provider); await model.providers.loadCatalog(provider, force: true) } }` with the comment "Only an edit counts: loading the stored key into the field must not save or check it."

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:768-771 - `.onAppear { binaryPath = model.settings.binaryPath(for: provider); if provider.acceptsAPIKey { apiKey = model.settings.apiKeyInput(for: provider) } }`

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:796-799 - `.onChange(of: model.settings.apiKeyInput(for: provider)) { _, value in guard provider.acceptsAPIKey, value != apiKey else { return }; apiKey = value }`
requirements.preconditions: A provider section with a key field is showing.
requirements.action: The user types in the key field.
requirements.expected_result: The field is populated from the stored key when the section first appears, and that population does NOT count as an edit: the guard compares the field against the stored value, so no write and no check happen. A real edit writes the key immediately (which persists it) and then schedules a check 600 milliseconds later. Each keystroke cancels the pending check and schedules a new one, so a burst of typing produces exactly one check. When it runs, it refreshes the provider's status and then force-reloads its model catalog. A change made to the stored key from elsewhere is mirrored back into the field, guarded so it does not loop.
side_effects: Persists the key immediately

requirements.preconditions: A release's notes are being parsed.
requirements.expected_result: Nil or empty notes give an empty digest. The same raw text as last time returns the cached digest. Otherwise the text is walked line by line, each line trimmed of spaces: blank lines, a bare "---" and any line starting with "<" are skipped. A line whose first character is one of the seven bullet markers and whose second is a space or a tab is a bullet; it is dropped when no category is current, and otherwise has its links, bold and inline code stripped in that order (each replaced by its captured text, then trimmed of spaces and tabs) and is appended if what remains is non-empty. A heading that matches one of the nine accepted names, case-insensitively and after stripping hashes, bold markers, spaces, tabs and colons, becomes the current category; the accepted names are "new features" and "new"; "bug fixes", "fixes" and "bugs"; "refinements" and "improvements". Any other heading clears the current category, so bullets under a "Thanks to contributors" heading are left out. A heading is a line of one or more hashes followed by nothing, a space or a tab, or a line wrapped in double asterisks longer than four characters; a plain sentence ending in a colon is not a heading. Then, for each of the three categories in declaration order, an empty one is omitted, duplicates are removed case-insensitively keeping the first occurrence, and if the last remaining bullet contains a numeric word immediately before a word that reduces to "extra", that bullet becomes the section's rollup and its number is added to the change count rather than being listed as a change.
requirements.persistence: None; the memo is in-memory and holds only the last parse.
failure_cases: Notes in no recognised shape: the digest is empty and the page shows the raw notes as markdown instead.

requirements.preconditions: An install is reporting progress, or the post-relaunch sweep is running.
requirements.expected_result: A pill track 14 points tall with a 20-point head. The displayed fraction chases the reported target once per display frame at up to 60 frames a second, exponentially, never going backwards except by snapping when the target itself drops. The frame clock is paused as soon as the displayed value reaches the target, and while anything in the app is scrolling, and restarts when the target moves. The chase is seeded with the target's current value at mount, so the post-relaunch sweep does not open from zero. The fill is a three-stop blue gradient anchored to the whole track and revealed by a leading clip, fading in between fractions 0.012 and 0.05 on a smoothstep; 14 sparkles twinkle in the filled part from a deterministic field and are suppressed entirely under Reduce Motion. The whole control is one accessibility element labelled the verbatim "Updating Marrow" (OD-0012 F1; upstream "Updating Droppy Code") whose value is the fraction as a whole-number percentage. During the celebration phase the chase uses a slower response of 0.72 with a minimum speed of 0.12 so the sweep is visible; otherwise 0.3 with no floor; Reduce Motion uses 0.15 in both cases.

requirements.preconditions: A row is grabbed and a pointer move has been delivered.
requirements.action: The visual offset exceeds half the sum of the grabbed row's slot and the next neighbour's slot, in either direction.
requirements.expected_result: The neighbour and the grabbed row swap. The test is a strict greater-than against `(own + slot) / 2 + slot * pastCentre`, with pastCentre zero in the sidebar, so the swap fires the moment the centre is crossed. The loop repeats, so one fast flick can cross several rows in a single delivery. If the move closure returns false the loop breaks without advancing the index and without adding the compensation. Each accepted swap adds or subtracts the neighbour's slot height from `settled`, which keeps the row pinned under the pointer while the list flows around it. The compensation must be applied inside `settle`, not inside the move closure, because `settle` mutates a copy of the caller's state.
side_effects: Each accepted swap writes the model through the move closure.
failure_cases: Grabbed id not in `order`: returns false immediately and nothing moves.
Move refused: loop stops there, leaving earlier swaps in place.
requirements.windows_path: Direct translation of the arithmetic. A void-returning move callback would reorder forever past a refused move (port_impacts 154), so the Bool return is mandatory. The fallback height is the literal 29 (Chrome.rowHeight 28 plus the list's 1 pt spacing).

requirements.preconditions: persistenceEnabled is true.
requirements.action: Any library mutation (project added, thread renamed, thread pinned, order changed).
requirements.expected_result: A mutation while persistenceEnabled is true and no save is pending schedules one: wait max(400 ms, 4 s minus the time since the last save), where 'time since the last save' is assumed to be 60 s when there has been none this run. That 60 s assumption always loses to the 400 ms floor in the max, so with no prior save the wait is 400 ms, never up to 60 s. A mutation while a save is already pending does nothing extra; that pending save carries it. When the wait ends, a fresh Library value is built from the current projects and threads and handed to the disk writer, which coalesces it against any snapshot already waiting for library.json. Every saveLibrary() call, whether reached through this scheduler or called directly, stamps lastLibrarySave.
side_effects: Background write of library.json
Updates the lastLibrarySave timestamp that throttles the next scheduled save
requirements.persistence: library.json, written by the background writer after the debounce.
failure_cases: persistenceEnabled false (set by saveBeforeQuit) makes both scheduleSave and saveLibrary return without writing.
After a failed load of library.json in the same run (PR-STORE-013, OD-0008 A10), the save writes nothing to library.json; upstream writes the empty library over it.
A call to scheduleSave while saveTask is already non-nil is a complete no-op: it neither cancels nor restarts anything.
requirements.cancellation: The scheduled task is cancelled only by saveBeforeQuit; a later scheduleSave call while one is pending does not cancel it. A cancelled task writes nothing.
requirements.windows_path: Same 400 ms floor, same 4 s minimum spacing measured from lastLibrarySave, and the same per-file coalescing. The literals (400 ms, 4 s, 60 s fallback) must stay exact. Windows: PA-0015 applies - file replace, delete and rename can fail transiently with a sharing violation, so the operation retries with backoff, clears the read-only attribute before a delete, uses an atomic replace primitive and surfaces a real error after a bounded number of attempts rather than dropping the write.
