requirements.b3_note: scheduleSave is no longer a cancel-and-restart 400 ms debounce. It now returns early while a save is already pending (no cancellation, no restart), and the wait is max(400 ms, 4 s minus the time since the last save, where that time-since is assumed to be 60 s when there has been none) - which always resolves to the 400 ms floor when there has been no prior save, not to 60 s - so a burst of changes writes once 400 ms after the FIRST change of the burst rather than 400 ms after the last, and a steady stream of changes is no longer starved (no write at all, as the old cancel-and-restart could produce). Every saveLibrary() call, including the direct ones from settle/reopen/delete, stamps lastLibrarySave, so a scheduled save that follows one of those waits up to 4 s from it. saveBeforeQuit does NOT call saveLibrary and does NOT stamp lastLibrarySave; it writes library.json synchronously through its own separate path (AppModel.swift:1327-1345). Upstream commit (bootstrap CLI self-update change) fixed a September 22 incident where a busy Hydra team rewrote library.json over two gigabytes in an hour and a quarter. Review fix (finding #5, MEDIUM): the 60 s figure and the saveBeforeQuit/scheduled-save stamping claims were previously misstated in this file's sibling record, PR-LAUNCH-076; both were corrected there and the same correction is reflected here and in E:/Droppy/work/b3/B3_PLAN.md section A32.

requirements.preconditions: None.
requirements.expected_result: Dates are written as ISO 8601 strings. Object keys are emitted in Foundation's .sortedKeys order (Coding.swift:23), which keeps successive saves byte-stable; that order is Foundation's own, and an ordinal code-unit sort is not evidence of it. Pretty printing is not enabled, so the file is one line. Forward slashes are escaped as \/ by the Foundation encoder, whose default this is. The attachment sweep does not depend on the escaping: its pattern makes the backslash optional (Storage.swift:118), so it matches the escaped and the unescaped form alike. The encoder is Foundation's JSONEncoder on macOS 26.0 or later, the deployment target (project.yml:5); its key collation, its escaping of non-ASCII and control characters and its formatting of Double values are Foundation internals that no pinned file states. The verifier's reading of Foundation (keys compared with [.numeric, .caseInsensitive, .forcedOrdering]; every non-C0 scalar written as raw UTF-8; other C0 controls as \u00XX with lowercase hex; Doubles from Double.description, such as 1e+16 and 1e-05) was not run on macOS and is UNVERIFIED (UNK-0003); the byte-compare fixture settles each point before it is asserted.
requirements.persistence: The wire format of library.json and every thread file.
requirements.windows_path: One shared serializer configured for ISO 8601 dates, sorted keys, no pretty printing and slash escaping. Slash escaping is kept because it is the encoder's default output, not because the sweep needs it (the sweep matches both forms, Storage.swift:118). The key comparer, the non-ASCII and control-character escaping and the number format must reproduce Foundation's JSONEncoder; an ordinal key sort and a relaxed escaper are not evidence of parity, and each is pinned only by the macOS-produced fixture.

requirements.preconditions: Thread files exist.
requirements.expected_result: Only files whose name ends in ".json" are scanned. The pattern looks for the literal "attachments", an optional backslash, a forward slash, then a 36-character run of hex digits and dashes, a dot and one or more alphanumerics; the captured group is the bare file name, which is inserted into the referenced set. The optional backslash exists because the storage encoder escapes forward slashes as \/ inside the persisted absolute path.
failure_cases: A thread file that cannot be read is skipped with continue, so every attachment referenced only by that thread becomes a sweep candidate and will be deleted once it is a day old. This is source behaviour and is reproduced.
requirements.windows_path: On Windows the persisted path separator is a backslash, so the stored path reads attachments\\<uuid>.<ext> in JSON (a literal backslash, escaped). The pattern MUST be adjusted to match the separator the Windows encoder actually writes, or the sweep matches nothing and every attachment is deleted a day after it is written. This is the single highest-risk line in the area: the writer’s separator and the sweeper’s pattern must be changed together, exactly as port_impacts.md entry 81 warns for the worktree slug.

requirements.preconditions: Two texts within the size cap.
requirements.expected_result: Both texts are split on "\n"; an empty string yields an empty line array, not one empty line. newLines.difference(from: oldLines) gives the removed old-line offsets and inserted new-line offsets. When neither set has a member the result is diff nil, additions 0, deletions 0 (identical inputs, including two empty texts). Otherwise both texts are walked together into one merged stream of context/deletion/addition ops, numbered from one on whichever side they belong to (a deletion has only an old number, an addition only a new number, context has both). The change ops (deletions and additions) are grouped into hunks: a change starts a new hunk unless its position in the op stream is at most 2*contextLines+1 = 7 past the previous change in the same group, in which case it extends the current group. Each hunk takes 3 ops of context before its first change and 3 after its last, clamped to the stream, and its header is "@@ -<oldStart>,<oldCount> +<newStart>,<newCount> @@" where oldStart/newStart are the first old/new number in the hunk's slice (0 when the slice has no op on that side) and oldCount/newCount are how many ops in the slice carry that side's number; the count is always printed, even for 1 or 0. The hunk's body lines are the slice's ops rendered as " " (context), "-" (deletion) or "+" (addition) followed by the line text. Multiple hunks are joined with "\n", and there are no "---"/"+++" file header lines.

Where CollectionDifference.difference(from:) has more than one minimal edit script for the same pair of texts, the ops chosen follow Swift stdlib tie-breaking, which needs pinned evidence (fixtures captured from the reference build, or the stdlib source at the toolchain tag) rather than assumption - UNRESOLVED.

[Marrow anti-slop guidance]
Give the shortest complete answer, leading with the result. Use plain, natural language. Skip filler, hype, stock openings, repeated summaries and unsolicited closers. Preserve requested detail, facts, uncertainty, blockers and required validation.
Make focused edits using existing patterns. Add comments only for non-obvious reasons, constraints or pitfalls; omit banners, obvious narration and speculative TODOs. Preserve useful documentation. Avoid unrelated cleanup, dependencies and abstractions.

Apply this guidance to delegated work too. Report changes, affected files and material limits once. User requests and project requirements take precedence.

requirements.preconditions: A recipe has been matched to a concrete model.

DroppyCode/Core/Support/Coding.swift:5-7 - func value<T: Decodable>(_ key: Key, default fallback: @autoclosure () -> T) -> T { ((try? decodeIfPresent(T.self, forKey: key)) ?? nil) ?? fallback() }, so a missing key, an explicit null and a type mismatch all collapse onto the fallback
requirements.preconditions: A stored thread record in library.json whose "effort" key is absent, null, or of the wrong JSON type.
requirements.action: The library is decoded at app launch.

requirements.windows_path: Nullable free-text field; do not narrow it to an enum, or an effort written by a newer build is silently dropped on load.
requirements.verification_method: unit test decoding a thread record that carries only id and projectID, plus one carrying the key as null and one carrying it as the wrong JSON type, asserting the same result in all three

DroppyCode/Core/Support/ISO8601.swift:23-26 - /// A bare date with no time; `nil` for anything else. static func dateOnly(from text: String) -> Date? { try? dateOnly.parse(text) }
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CopilotSession.swift:470-472 - private static func parseDate(_ text: String) -> Date? { ISO8601.date(from: text) ?? ISO8601.dateOnly(from: text) }
requirements.preconditions: A date string such as `2026-09-13`, as GitHub Copilot's quota endpoint writes it.
requirements.expected_result: The text is parsed with a private static style built from Date.ISO8601FormatStyle() limited to year, month and day. A match returns that date; anything else returns nil and nothing throws. ISO8601.date(from:) does not accept this shape, so a caller that wants it must ask for it: the only caller at B2 is CopilotSession.parseDate, which tries the full stamp first and the bare date second. The instant returned follows the style's default time zone.
failure_cases: Anything the year-month-day style does not parse returns nil.

UNRESOLVED (UNK-0003, no matching-build macOS runtime to run Foundation on): the default time zone of Date.ISO8601FormatStyle() (UTC in Foundation's documented initializer) and whether trailing text after the day is rejected were not run; the fixture settles both.
requirements.windows_path: A separate date-only parser, never merged into the full-stamp parser, so a bare date is accepted only where the source asks for it. Midnight in the fixture-confirmed time zone of the Foundation style.
requirements.verification_method: unit test: `2026-09-13` parses to the fixture-confirmed instant, `2026-09-13T18:28:42Z`-style input goes through CopilotSession.parseDate's first branch, and `13/09/2026` and `` return null

requirements.title: Each project and thread gets its own cell, built in the app model's initializer and written only when its item changes
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:138-141 - comment "Property observers stay quiet inside an initializer, so the cells are built here once." then Self.write(Self.sync(&projectCells, with: projects)), Self.write(Self.sync(&threadCells, with: threads)), syncChildCells()

DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:149-151 - doc comment "Mirrors a list into its cells: values that changed are written to their cell (and only those, so an untouched item's observers never fire), new items get a cell, and a removed item's cell is emptied as it goes, so whoever was showing it re-renders to nothing."

DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:158-178 - sync(_:with:): if let cell = cells[value.id] reuses the cell and writes only if cell.value != value (:166-167); cells[value.id] = ObservedValue(value) is the only creation (:169); an unseen id gets a nil write and is dropped (:172-176)
DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:30-32 - projects didSet { Self.write(Self.sync(&projectCells, with: projects)) }
requirements.preconditions: The library holds projects and threads.
requirements.action: The app model is created from the stored library; later one thread is renamed, the list is reassigned with that thread unchanged, or the thread is removed.
requirements.expected_result: Each item's cell is created once per item. Cells are built inside AppModel.init because property observers do not fire there. On every later change to the list, values that changed are written to their cell, and only those, so an untouched item's observers never fire; new items get a cell; a removed item's cell is emptied as it goes, so whoever was showing it re-renders to nothing.
requirements.windows_path: The constructor builds the cells explicitly after loading, because a C# constructor assigns backing fields and runs no didSet (R-OBS-1, R-OBS-2). The dictionary is settled before the cells are written (R-OBS-5). An unchanged item's cell is not written, which matters because ObservedValue notifies on every assignment (R-OBS-3, SetAlways).
requirements.verification_method: unit test on AppModel with a library fixture. Right after construction, project(id) and thread(id) return every loaded item. A tracker on thread(A) (which reads through A's cell, AppModel.swift:297-299) fires once when A is renamed through the model, and still fires on a second rename, which shows the cell was not replaced. It does not fire when thread B is renamed or when the list is reassigned with A unchanged. When A is removed, the tracker fires and thread(A) is nil.

requirements.preconditions: A value has been handed to DiskWriter.shared.encodeAndWrite(_:to:) and its queued hop has run.
requirements.action: A caller asks lastWrittenSize(of:) for that URL.
requirements.expected_result: lastWrittenSize(of:) returns the byte count of the value's last successful write made through encodeAndWrite for that URL, or nil for a file never written that way. Only encodeAndWrite's queued hop records a size, and only on success (write(_:to:) returning non-nil). writeSynchronously, removeSynchronously, a failed encode and a failed write all leave the stored size exactly as it was.
side_effects: Records the write's byte size in an in-memory map, keyed by URL
requirements.persistence: In-memory only, under a Mutex; not written to disk and not read back across launches.
failure_cases: A failed encode or a failed write leaves the previously recorded size (or the absence of one) unchanged.
writeSynchronously and removeSynchronously never update or clear the recorded size for that URL, even though they touch the same file.
requirements.windows_path: Direct port: the same per-URL map (Mutex<[URL: Int]>), updated only from the asynchronous encodeAndWrite path, read by lastWrittenSize(of:).
requirements.verification_method: unit: encodeAndWrite a value, wait for the queued hop to run, assert lastWrittenSize(of:) equals the encoded byte count; assert a subsequent writeSynchronously or removeSynchronously for the same URL does not change the recorded size; assert an unencodable value leaves lastWrittenSize as it was

requirements.preconditions: Two texts that compare equal line by line under Swift String ==, including the case where both are empty.
requirements.expected_result: newLines.difference(from: oldLines) has no removed and no inserted offsets, so unified returns FileEdit.Stats(diff: nil, additions: 0, deletions: 0) immediately, before the merged-ops walk or any hunk work runs. Lines are compared as produced by splitting each text on "\n" (an empty string gives an empty line array). Downstream, the nil diff is not uniformly invisible: the tool row's own inline rendering shows no diff block for it (TimelineRows.swift:2128), and DiffInspector's focusedFiles fallback contributes nothing for it (DiffInspector.swift:165, which requires a non-nil, non-empty patch); but on a tool row that is part of the selected turn, TurnDiff.merge (TurnDiff.swift:39-48) still appends this edit as a hunk-less DiffFile (it filters only on an empty path, not a nil diff, and only records reportedAdditions/reportedDeletions when file.hunks.isEmpty), so DiffInspector's file card still appears for it, reading "Diff details unavailable" rather than showing a diff (DiffInspector.swift:215-221), and the tool row still opens the changes popover because TimelineRows.swift's opensDiff (:1664-1665) is true whenever the call has any edit with a non-empty path, independent of whether that edit's own diff is nil.
requirements.persistence: Nothing is stored for such an edit: no diff text, and the recorded additions and deletions are both 0.
failure_cases: A reported edit with a nil diff renders no diff block in the tool row's own inline rendering (TimelineRows.swift:2128) and DiffInspector's focusedFiles fallback adds nothing for it (DiffInspector.swift:165).

But when that same edit's path is part of the selected turn's own diff, TurnDiff.merge (TurnDiff.swift:39-48) still adds a hunk-less file for it, so the inspector shows a "Diff details unavailable" card (DiffInspector.swift:215-221) rather than no card, and the tool row still opens the changes popover (TimelineRows.swift:1664-1665) rather than staying collapsed.
ThreadRuntime.swift:3447 settleCommand treats such an edit as unreported, so the git-snapshot edits replace it rather than leaving a phantom empty diff.
requirements.windows_path: Reproduce the short-circuit and its two downstream effects: a nil diff must render no diff block at all (not an empty one), and must not stop the git-snapshot edits from replacing the report.
requirements.verification_method: unit: two identical multi-line texts and two empty texts both give diff nil, additions 0, deletions 0; integration test that a tool row carrying such an edit shows no diff block and that DiffInspector shows none
requirements.title: Identical texts produce no diff hunk and zero additions and deletions
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Text.swift:105-115 - removed/inserted offset sets built from newLines.difference(from: oldLines); guard !removed.isEmpty || !inserted.isEmpty else { return FileEdit.Stats(diff: nil, additions: 0, deletions: 0) }

requirements.preconditions: A session is being created with a startup command.
requirements.expected_result: Upstream: the arguments are exactly ["-l", "-i", "-c", <fourth>] in that order, four elements, never three and never five. The fourth is built by string interpolation as the command, then "; exec ", then the SHELL'S OWN ABSOLUTE PATH, then " -l": the same path used as the executable, not the bare shell name. Neither the command nor the path is quoted or escaped, so the command runs as written and a shell path containing a space would break the exec. The trailing exec replaces the shell with a fresh login shell instead of letting the tab exit when the script finishes, and it runs whether the command succeeded or failed, because the two are joined by a semicolon rather than by &&. DEVIATION (OD-0008 C5): the port runs the script in PowerShell 7 if installed, otherwise Windows PowerShell. The source intent kept is: run the command as written, then leave an interactive shell in the same tab whether it succeeded or failed. The exact PowerShell argument vector is not fixed by the ruling or the source and remains an engineering decision to record before this is SPECIFIED.
side_effects: The command runs with the user's full login environment and profile, in the project directory
failure_cases: A command containing an unbalanced quote, a stray semicolon or a trailing backslash changes what the composed line means; the source does no escaping
A shell path containing a space breaks the exec and the tab exits when the script ends (upstream)
The command failing does not stop the hand-back: the tab still becomes an interactive shell

source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:524-532 addProject(at:) - an existing project with the same standardized path is returned unchanged; otherwise a new Project is made and project.scripts = ProjectFile.scripts(at: url) before it is appended and a save is scheduled

DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:1348-1363 ProjectFile.scripts(at:) - reads Data from url.appendingPathComponent("droppy-code.json"), parses it as JSON, takes json["scripts"] as an array, and for each entry requires a string "name" and a string "command", mapping "icon" through symbol(for:) and reading "runOnWorktreeCreate" as a bool defaulting to false
requirements.preconditions: A folder is being added as a project for the first time.
requirements.expected_result: If droppy-code.json exists at the project root and parses, every entry of its scripts array that has both a string name and a string command becomes a ProjectScript; entries missing either are silently skipped. The file's "icon" string is mapped to an SF Symbol name (PR-TERM-061) and "runOnWorktreeCreate" is read as a bool, defaulting to false. A missing, unreadable or unparseable file yields an empty list with no message. This import happens only when the project is first added: re-adding the same path returns the existing project and does NOT re-read the file, and nothing re-reads it later.
side_effects: One file read; the library save is scheduled.
requirements.persistence: The imported scripts become part of the persisted project record, so later edits in the editor diverge from the file and are not written back to it.
failure_cases: File absent, unreadable or invalid JSON: empty list, no error shown.
An entry without a name or without a command: that entry is skipped silently.
requirements.windows_path: Same file name at the project root and the same tolerant parse: OD-0008 B13 keeps reading droppy-code.json, so existing Droppy projects work. This matches upstream and is not a deviation.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture with a droppy-code.json holding valid, partial and malformed entries

requirements.preconditions: An executable URL is known.
requirements.expected_result: The process runs off the main actor. With no directory argument the child inherits the app's own working directory rather than being given one. With no environment argument it gets LoginEnvironment.current. With no input, stdin is the null device, so a child that reads stdin sees EOF immediately rather than blocking. The result carries the raw exit status and both streams as Data; text accessors decode UTF-8 lossily via String(decoding:as:).
side_effects: A child process is launched.
failure_cases: process.run() throws (missing or non-executable file): the error is rethrown to the caller through the continuation and no result is produced.
requirements.windows_path: CreateProcess-equivalent with three pipes and NUL as stdin when there is no input. Platform boundary: Windows has no direct equivalent of inheriting the parent's cwd selectively, and the child must be given an explicit environment block.

requirements.title: A command that outlives its timeout is terminated; the default timeout is 120 seconds
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:42 - timeout: TimeInterval = 120 is the default parameter

requirements.preconditions: A command is running.
requirements.expected_result: The process is terminated (PR-TERM-085) and the call returns with whatever exit status the termination produced, which is non-zero, so ShellResult.succeeded is false. The deadline task is cancelled as soon as the process exits normally, and again on the way out, so a finished command never gets killed late.

requirements.title: Termination is a two-step ladder: terminate now, then kill the process group one second later if it is still running
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:110-118 terminate(_:) - returns unless the process is running; calls process.terminate(); then on a global .utility queue one second later, if it is still running, calls kill with -pid when getpgid(pid) == pid and with pid otherwise, sending SIGKILL
porting/critiques/triage_summary.json:92 - notes that neither call site uses setsid, so whether the group dies depends on the child
requirements.preconditions: A process is running and must stop.
requirements.action: terminate is called by the timeout or by cancellation.
requirements.expected_result: SIGTERM first. Exactly one second later, if the process is still alive, SIGKILL is sent to the whole process group when the process is its own group leader, and to the single process otherwise. The one-second gap and the group-leader test are both load-bearing: a child that is not a group leader has only itself killed, so its own children survive.
side_effects: Signals are delivered; grandchildren may or may not die depending on the group test.
failure_cases: A child that is not a group leader can leave grandchildren running. This is upstream behaviour and is not repaired.
requirements.windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY. Windows has no signals and no process groups in this sense. The closest faithful shape is a graceful stop request followed one second later by a forced termination, with the tree-versus-single distinction resolved by a Job Object. Whether the port kills the tree or only the process must be an explicit engineering decision that records the difference from the source, not a silent choice.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture with a child that spawns a grandchild
requirements.open_question: No ruling is missing: ED-047 (Q127) decides this ladder on Windows (own Job Object per child, CTRL_BREAK_EVENT to the child's process group, TerminateJobObject one second later). This record's windows_path predates ED-047 and was not rewritten; ED-047 is outside the decisions this maintenance pass applies (OD-0012 to OD-0014, ED-059 to ED-063), so the record stays DISCOVERED until a pass writes ED-047 into it.

requirements.title: After the process exits, output collection is awaited with a three-second grace and then forced closed

requirements.title: Supplied stdin data is written on a background queue and the handle is closed afterwards, with both errors swallowed
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:90-95 - when input and stdin both exist, a DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated) block does try? write(contentsOf: input) then try? close()
requirements.preconditions: Shell.run was called with input data.

requirements.windows_path: Same background write and close, with the same error suppression.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture piping a large input to a child that exits early

requirements.title: The login environment is captured once by running the user's shell as an interactive login shell around a marked env dump, with an 8-second budget
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:367-385 read() - marker "__DROPPY_CODE_ENVIRONMENT__"; script is printf of the marker, then /usr/bin/env -0, then printf of the marker; the shell is run with ["-l", "-i", "-c", script] with the fallback environment and timeout 8; the region strictly between the first and last marker occurrence is split on NUL; each entry is split at its first '='

requirements.preconditions: The app is starting.
requirements.expected_result: The user's shell runs its login and interactive profiles and prints its whole environment NUL-separated between two copies of the marker. Only the region between the first and the last marker is parsed, and only when the first ends before the last begins, so profile output before or after the dump is ignored. Entries with an empty key or a key in the excluded set are dropped. Entries with no '=' are skipped. Values may contain '=' because only the first one splits. The whole read is abandoned after 8 seconds, leaving the fallback environment.
side_effects: The user's shell profile files are executed, which can have arbitrary effects.
One child process.
requirements.persistence: None on disk; the result is cached in memory for the run.
failure_cases: The shell fails, times out, or prints no markers: the fallback environment is used with only the PATH augmentation applied.
requirements.windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY, unresolved. Windows processes inherit the user environment directly, so the login-shell read has no purpose (porting/platform_adaptations.md:206-207). What replaces it is the engineering decision PA-0009 calls for (porting/platform_adaptations.md:206-214), and none is recorded in porting/engineering_decisions.md. One candidate, not yet decided, is a read of the process environment plus the user and machine Environment registry keys.

requirements.title: Softness blurs with a radius of softness times 28, clamped at the edges so the frame stays solid
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift:247-248 the doc comment: 'Softens the base picture per `softness`, scaled by `radiusScale` so a smaller copy gets a proportionally smaller radius. Runs anywhere: Core Image does the work.'
DroppyCode/UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift:250-251 `let radius = softness * 28 * radiusScale` and `guard radius > 0.01 else { return base }`
DroppyCode/UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift:252 `guard let blur = CIFilter(name: "CIGaussianBlur") else { return base }` - the filter identity is the literal string "CIGaussianBlur"

DroppyCode/UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift:253-254 comment: "The blur shrinks opaque edges toward transparent, so the image is clamped first and cropped back to its own extent: the middle softens while the frame stays solid."

DroppyCode/UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift:255-259 `let extent = CGRect(origin: .zero, size: CGSize(width: base.width, height: base.height))`, `blur.setValue(CIImage(cgImage: base).clampedToExtent(), forKey: kCIInputImageKey)`, `blur.setValue(radius, forKey: kCIInputRadiusKey)`, `guard let output = blur.outputImage?.cropped(to: extent) else { return nil }`, `return ciContext.createCGImage(output, from: extent)`
DroppyCode/UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift:26 `nonisolated static let ciContext = CIContext(options: [.useSoftwareRenderer: false])` with the comment that making one per picture stalls the softness slider
requirements.preconditions: A downsampled base picture exists.
requirements.action: The picture is softened for a softness value.
requirements.expected_result: The Gaussian radius is softness multiplied by 28 and by the radius scale (1 for the full-size render, the preview-to-base width ratio for a live preview). A radius of 0.01 or less returns the base unchanged, so softness 0 costs nothing. The filter is created by name, and the name is exactly "CIGaussianBlur"; the input image is set under kCIInputImageKey and the radius under kCIInputRadiusKey. The source is clamped to its own extent before blurring and the result cropped back to that extent, taken as the origin plus the base image's pixel width and height, so the picture's outer pixels stay opaque instead of fading to transparent at the window edges. One shared GPU-backed render context is used for every blur, never one per picture.
side_effects: GPU image work
failure_cases: The blur filter cannot be created: the base is returned unblurred.
The filter produces no output: nothing is returned, and the caller drops the render.
requirements.windows_path: Platform boundary: "CIGaussianBlur" is a Core Image filter identifier with no Windows counterpart, so the Windows build substitutes its own Gaussian blur (Direct2D's Gaussian blur effect or equivalent). The filter's IDENTITY is recorded here so the substitution is a named one rather than a guess, and so the radius semantics can be matched: Core Image's radius parameter is the Gaussian's standard-deviation-derived radius, and a Windows blur whose parameter means something else must be converted rather than passed through. The 28 multiplier, the 0.01 short-circuit, and the clamp-then-crop edge handling are all observable and must match; a blur without edge clamping puts a soft translucent band around the whole window.
requirements.verification_method: unit: radius formula and the short-circuit; capture comparison: the picture's corner pixels stay opaque at softness 1

requirements.title: The tone generator sums notes of exponentially decaying partials over a raised-cosine attack
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Sound/ToneSynth.swift:7-19 Note (frequency, onset, level) and Partial (multiple, level, decay)
DroppyCode/UI/Sound/ToneSynth.swift:22-23 `private static let attack = 0.006` with the comment "A raised-cosine onset: quick enough to feel struck, with no click."

DroppyCode/UI/Sound/ToneSynth.swift:27-40 the loop: `let count = Int(sampleRate * duration)`; per note `let start = Int(note.onset * sampleRate)`; for each index from start, `time = Double(index - start) / sampleRate`, `onset = time < attack ? 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(.pi * time / attack) : 1`, `tone = sum over partials of partial.level * exp(-time / partial.decay) * sin(2 * .pi * note.frequency * partial.multiple * time)`, `samples[index] += note.level * onset * tone`
requirements.preconditions: A note list, a partial list and a duration are given.
requirements.expected_result: The buffer holds floor(44100 times duration) samples. Each note starts at floor(onset times 44100) and runs to the end of the buffer. Within a note, the envelope is 0.5 minus 0.5 times cos(pi times t / 0.006) for the first 6 milliseconds and 1 afterwards. The note's timbre at time t is the sum over its partials of level times exp(-t / decay) times sin(2 pi f multiple t), where f is the note's own frequency. Notes are summed into the same buffer, so overlapping notes add.
failure_cases: None expressed in source.
requirements.windows_path: Pure arithmetic; port it directly in double precision. The partial set is shared by every note of a chime, not per note.
requirements.verification_method: unit: sample-by-sample comparison against the formula for a known note and partial list

DroppyCode/UI/Sound/ToneSynth.swift:45-46 `let peak = samples.reduce(0) { max($0, abs($1)) }` and `let scale = peak > 0 ? 0.9 / peak : 0`
DroppyCode/UI/Sound/ToneSynth.swift:66-67 `append(Int16((sample * scale * Double(Int16.max)).rounded()))`

requirements.action: The tone is finished and written out.

Samples are converted with round-half-away-from-zero to signed 16-bit using 32767 as full scale, so the peak sample is 29490.

requirements.title: A table is a line containing a pipe whose next line is a delimiter row, and it runs until a blank or pipe-free line
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:154-168 the table branch: requires a next line, the current trimmed line to contain "|", and `isTableDelimiter(lines[index + 1])`; the header is the current line's cells; the index advances by two; rows are taken while the trimmed line is non-empty and contains "|"
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:325-329 `isTableDelimiter(_ line:)`: the trimmed line must contain "-" and every character must be one of '|', ':', '-' or ' '

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:331-337 `tableCells(_ line:)`: trims the line, drops one leading '|' and one trailing '|', splits on '|' keeping empty pieces, and trims each cell of whitespace
requirements.preconditions: A line contains a pipe and is followed by another line.
requirements.action: The parser tests for a table.
requirements.expected_result: The next line must contain at least one dash and consist only of pipes, colons, dashes and spaces. When it does, the current line is the header row and the delimiter line is consumed. Body rows continue while lines are non-empty and contain a pipe. Cells are produced by trimming the line, removing one leading and one trailing pipe, splitting on pipes without dropping empties, and trimming each cell. Alignment colons in the delimiter row are parsed for the purpose of recognising the row but are otherwise discarded: no alignment is carried into the block.
failure_cases: A delimiter row with no dash is not a delimiter, so the pair renders as paragraphs.
Rows with more or fewer cells than the header are kept as they are; the renderer pads short rows (PR-THEME-119).
requirements.windows_path: Column alignment is parsed away and never applied. Every cell renders leading-aligned regardless of the colons; that is the shipped behaviour.
requirements.verification_method: unit: a table with alignment colons renders leading-aligned; ragged rows; a pipe line with no delimiter

requirements.title: A bullet marker is a dash, asterisk or plus followed by a space or tab; an ordered marker is up to nine digits then a dot or a bracket
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:272-289 `listMarker(_ line:)`: for the first non-indent character in "-*+", the rest must start with a space or tab; the content is the rest with leading spaces and tabs dropped; contentOffset is indent + 2. Otherwise the leading digits must be non-empty and at most 9, the next character must be '.' or ')', and what follows must start with a space or be empty; the content is the remainder with leading spaces dropped; the start number is the digits as an integer or 1; contentOffset is indent + digit count + 2
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:291-297 `indentation(_ line:)`: a space counts 1, a tab counts 4, anything else stops the count
requirements.preconditions: A line is being tested for a list item.
requirements.expected_result: Indentation is measured with tabs worth four spaces. An unordered marker is one of dash, asterisk or plus followed immediately by a space or a tab; a marker followed by any other character is not a marker. An ordered marker is one to nine digits followed by a dot or a closing bracket, then a space or the end of the line, so "1." alone on a line is an item with empty content. Ten or more digits is not a marker. The start number of the list is the first item's digits.
failure_cases: Not a marker: the line becomes paragraph text.
requirements.windows_path: Note the asymmetry: an unordered marker accepts a tab after it, an ordered one accepts only a space or nothing.

requirements.title: A list starts only at a paragraph boundary, or for an unordered marker, or for an ordered list beginning at 1
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:170 `if depth < maxDepth, let marker = listMarker(line), paragraph.isEmpty || !marker.ordered || marker.start == 1`
requirements.preconditions: A line carries a list marker while a paragraph is being accumulated.
requirements.action: The parser decides whether to start a list.
requirements.expected_result: A list starts when no paragraph is open, or when the marker is unordered, or when it is an ordered marker whose number is 1. An ordered marker with a number other than 1 that appears in the middle of a paragraph does not start a list and stays as paragraph text, which is what keeps a sentence ending in "...in 2020. Next" from becoming a list.
failure_cases: None; the line falls through to the paragraph.
requirements.windows_path: Reproduce the three-part condition exactly; simplifying it changes how ordinary prose renders.
requirements.verification_method: unit: a paragraph line followed by "2. text" stays one paragraph; the same after a blank line becomes a list starting at 2

requirements.title: List items absorb following lines as continuation text or as nested child blocks, and a list ends when its kind changes
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:195-262 parseList: a marker at or above the first item's indent starts a new item, but only when its ordered flag matches the first item's, otherwise the list ends; a line indented past the first item's indent is dropped by the smaller of its indentation and the item's content offset and appended to the child lines, unless the child lines are still empty and the line is neither a marker nor a fence, in which case its trimmed form continues the item's own text; an unindented line continues the item's text only while there are no child lines and it is not a heading, a fence or a quote; anything else ends the list

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:222-234 a blank line is skipped when the next line is indented past the item (recorded as an empty child line) or when the next line is a sibling marker of the same indent and kind; otherwise it ends the list
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:214 each item's children are `parse(childLines[...], depth: depth + 1).blocks`
requirements.preconditions: A list has started.
requirements.action: The parser reads the lines after the first marker.
requirements.expected_result: Sibling items are markers at the same or a smaller indent with the same ordered flag; a marker of the other kind ends the list rather than continuing it. Indented lines become the item's nested blocks, parsed one level deeper, except that indented prose arriving before any nested block simply continues the item's text. Unindented lines continue the item's text only until the item has nested blocks, and never when they are a heading, a fence or a quote. A blank line does not end the list when the next line either is indented content or is a sibling marker; otherwise it does.
failure_cases: None expressed in source; every line either continues, nests or ends the list.
requirements.windows_path: This is the most intricate part of the grammar and the part a CommonMark library will get differently. It must be ported rule by rule and covered by fixtures.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture: a list corpus covering loose lists, nested code, mixed markers and blank lines

requirements.title: A list item beginning "[ ] " or "[x] " becomes a checkbox item, case-insensitively for x, and the marker is removed from its text
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:203-217 flushItem: the item's joined text is whitespace-trimmed, then `if text.hasPrefix("[ ] ") { checked = false; text.removeFirst(4) } else if text.lowercased().hasPrefix("[x] ") { checked = true; text.removeFirst(4) }`
requirements.preconditions: A list item's text has been gathered.
requirements.expected_result: An item whose text begins with exactly "[ ] " is unchecked; one beginning with "[x] " or "[X] " is checked. In both cases the first four characters are removed from the text. Any other bracket form, including "[]" with no space and "[ ]" with no following space, is left as ordinary text with no checkbox.
failure_cases: No match: checked stays absent and the item renders with its normal marker.
requirements.windows_path: Note the lower-casing is applied to the whole item text just to test the prefix, which is wasteful but harmless; only the prefix test is case-insensitive, the removal is a fixed four characters.

requirements.title: Paragraph lines accumulate until a blank line or another block starts, and a paragraph that trims to nothing is dropped
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:86-93 flushParagraph: `let text = paragraph.joined(separator: "\n").trimmed`; `if !text.isEmpty { blocks.append(.paragraph(text)); blockLines.append(paragraphStart) }`; `paragraph.removeAll()`
DroppyCode/Core/Support/Text.swift:222-224 `var trimmed: String { trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }`
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:99-103 a blank line flushes the paragraph
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:179-181 otherwise the raw (untrimmed) line is appended and the paragraph's start line is recorded on the first one
requirements.preconditions: A line is not any other block.
requirements.expected_result: Lines are kept with their original leading and trailing whitespace and joined with newlines; the joined text is then trimmed at both ends. A paragraph of only whitespace produces no block at all. Interior line breaks are preserved in the paragraph's text and are resolved later by the inline layer.

requirements.verification_method: unit: a two-line paragraph keeps its newline; a whitespace-only line produces nothing
requirements.b2_change: Re-cited only. MarkdownParser.swift:87 `.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` (B1) -> `.trimmed` (B2), which is the same trim (B2 Core/Support/Text.swift:132). Behaviour unchanged.

requirements.title: Line trimming takes a fast path for lines that begin and end with printable ASCII
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:264-270 `trimmed(_ line:)`: when the first and last UTF-8 bytes are both above 0x20 and below 0x7F the line is returned as it is; otherwise it is whitespace-trimmed
requirements.preconditions: A line is about to be tested.
requirements.expected_result: A line whose first and last bytes are printable ASCII other than space is used unchanged. Any other line is trimmed of the whitespace character set, which includes Unicode spaces. The fast path is observably equivalent because a leading byte above 0x20 and below 0x7F cannot be a space, a tab or the lead byte of a Unicode space.
failure_cases: An empty line has no first byte and takes the slow path, which returns an empty string.
requirements.windows_path: The fast path is an optimization with no behavioural difference; a port may trim unconditionally, but must trim the full Unicode whitespace set, not just ASCII.
requirements.verification_method: unit: a line surrounded by U+00A0 is trimmed; an ASCII line is returned identically

requirements.title: A finished message renders its blocks as prose runs and standalone blocks; a streaming one renders every block separately
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:25-45 `segments(_:)`: headings, paragraphs, lists and quotes accumulate into a prose run; code, tables and rules close the run and stand alone

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:63-102 the body: when not streaming, the segments are rendered as ProseRunView for a run and MarkdownBlockView for a standalone block; while streaming, every block is a MarkdownBlockView carrying `settled: index < stable` and the streaming environment set only on the last block; both arms use a VStack of alignment leading and spacing 12 and set the veiled environment for the whole message
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:9-23 the view is Equatable on text and the streaming flag, so finished replies are skipped entirely while a new reply streams
requirements.preconditions: A message is being rendered.
requirements.expected_result: Blocks are stacked leading-aligned with 12 points between them. A finished message groups consecutive headings, paragraphs, lists and quotes into one prose run rendered as a single text object, breaking the run at each code block, table or rule, which render as their own views. A streaming message renders every block on its own, marks blocks below the stable count as settled, and marks only the last block as streaming. The whole message is marked veiled while it streams, so every block dissolves its arriving text, not only the last.
failure_cases: None expressed in source.
requirements.windows_path: The two paths produce visibly different typography (the run path is one native text object, the block path is a stack of views), and a message swaps from one to the other when its stream ends. That swap is the shipped behaviour and must be reproduced, including the spacing being 12 in both.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test: a reply's layout when streaming and after it finishes; unit: the segment grouping

requirements.title: Blocks compare by content, except that two blocks both marked settled compare equal without looking at their content
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:278-298 MarkdownBlockView is Equatable: `nonisolated static func == (lhs: MarkdownBlockView, rhs: MarkdownBlockView) -> Bool { if lhs.settled, rhs.settled { return true }; return lhs.block == rhs.block }` (:295-298), with the comment (:280-283) that comparing every byte of every earlier block of the reply on every flush is work the flush does not need
requirements.preconditions: A streaming reply flushes.
requirements.expected_result: Two block views in the same position that are both settled are treated as identical without comparing their content; every other pair is compared by value. Because the parser guarantees a settled block cannot change (PR-THEME-091), the result is the same as a deep comparison.
failure_cases: If the stable count were wrong, stale content would be shown; the correctness of PR-THEME-091 is what makes this safe.
requirements.windows_path: An equality short-circuit keyed on the parser's stability claim. A port that diffs by value everywhere is behaviourally identical but slower on long replies.
requirements.verification_method: unit: two settled views compare equal even with different content, which is the documented contract
requirements.b2_change: Re-cited only: B1 MarkdownView.swift:278-299 -> B2 :278-298, one line shorter because B1 :287 `@Environment(\.chatZoom) private var zoom` was removed. The equality rule is unchanged.

requirements.title: Every block appears with the soft-appear transition, except the sent delegation card which leaves without one
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:47-56 `transition(for:)`: a code block whose lower-cased info string is a delegation info gets `.asymmetric(insertion: .softAppear, removal: .identity)`; everything else gets `.softAppear`

DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift:958-961 `static var softAppear: Animation { .smooth(duration: 0.32) }`

A code block whose info string is exactly "hydra", "hydra-sent" or "hydra-leaving" (compared lower-cased) leaves with no transition at all, because the card has already faded in place before its block is removed; only the text below it animates closing up.

requirements.verification_method: interaction test: a delegation block leaving a reply does not glide over the text below it

requirements.title: A code block whose info string is a delegation info renders through a registered card renderer, faded and inert while leaving, and as plain code before any renderer is registered
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:324-336 the code case: when the lower-cased info string is a delegation info AND `MarkdownDelegationCard.render` is non-nil, `delegationRenderer(code, info != "hydra")` with `.opacity(info == "hydra-leaving" ? 0 : 1)`, `.scaleEffect(info == "hydra-leaving" ? 0.98 : 1, anchor: .top)` and `.allowsHitTesting(info != "hydra-leaving")`; otherwise (no delegation info, or no renderer registered yet) a CodeBlock

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:505-509 `enum MarkdownDelegationCard { @MainActor static var render: ((String, Bool) -> AnyView)? }` - a process-global hook the App sets at launch, because the card is an App-level view UI cannot name
DroppyCode/App/AppDelegate.swift:14 - applicationDidFinishLaunching registers MarkdownDelegationCard.render before the main window is shown (LAUNCH area)
requirements.preconditions: A reply contains a fenced block with one of the three delegation info strings.
requirements.expected_result: Once MarkdownDelegationCard.render has been set (which happens before the main window ever shows, at launch), the block renders through that renderer rather than as code, with its body and a sent flag passed to it. The renderer is marked sent for the info strings "hydra-sent" and "hydra-leaving" and not sent for "hydra". For "hydra-leaving" the rendered card is drawn at zero opacity, scaled to 0.98 anchored at its top, and takes no clicks, while still occupying its full room. Before the renderer is registered (there is no observable window for this in the running app, since it is set at launch before any content renders, but the fallback exists in source) the block renders as an ordinary CodeBlock instead of throwing or showing nothing.
failure_cases: MarkdownDelegationCard.render is nil: the block renders as CodeBlock. None expressed in source for the card renderer itself; it is specified by the Hydra area.
requirements.windows_path: The three info strings are a protocol between the runtime and the renderer; the exact strings are load-bearing and the comparison is on the lower-cased info string. The port's UI layer likewise cannot name the App-level card type, so it needs the same process-global registration hook, set during startup before the main window is shown; a nil hook must render CodeBlock, matching source, never throw or omit the block.
requirements.verification_method: unit: the three strings select the card renderer when one is registered; a nil renderer falls back to CodeBlock; interaction test: a leaving card holds its room
requirements.b3_note: B3 replaces the direct `HydraDelegationBlock(json:sent:)` call with a registered closure hook, `MarkdownDelegationCard.render` (:505-509), set by AppDelegate at launch (:14, LAUNCH area) rather than constructed inline. This adds a new fallback state: while the hook is nil, the block renders as CodeBlock instead of the delegation card (R3-31 #2, folded into this reclassification per B3_PLAN 6.3; the LAUNCH area records the AppDelegate.swift:14 registration itself).

requirements.windows_path: UNRESOLVED pending owner decision O4 (drive-letter and UNC paths, and what a chat link may launch): Windows paths are `C:\...` or `C:/...`, not `/...`, so a literal port of the "/"-rooted check never fires on Windows and every link falls through to the generic opener, where a bare drive-letter string parses with scheme "C" and fails against ShellExecuteW. Recommendation B (decisions_draft.md O4): treat Windows absolute paths (`C:\...`, `C:/...`, the file-URL form `/C:/...`) as the local-file branch with the same `:line` suffix rule; never open a UNC path (`\\host\share`, `file://host/...`) from a chat link, as a named safety deviation; and reveal a locally-runnable file type in File Explorer rather than launching it, also a named safety deviation. The generic opener (ShellExecuteW) must otherwise refuse a relative or scheme-less string it cannot resolve, rather than guessing.

requirements.expected_result: The phase is first wrapped into [0, 1) by taking the remainder modulo 1 and adding 1 when the result is negative, so a negative phase (a cell lagging the wave) is valid input. requirements.preconditions: A flight has been queued and its view has appeared.
requirements.expected_result: The landing point is the flight's own target when it has one, and otherwise the fixed point x 24, y the canvas height minus 12, which is the archive corner at the bottom left of the window. A departure animates progress from 0 to 1 and an arrival animates the identical keyframes backwards from 1 to 0, so an arrival is the same flight reversed rather than a separate animation. The flat image is drawn at the source frame's size, positioned at that frame's centre, inside a canvas-sized top-leading frame. Progress drives a distortion effect calling the genie shader with three arguments in this order: the progress as a float, the source frame as a float4 of minX, minY, width, height, and the landing point as a float2. The effect's maximum sample offset is the distance from the frame's centre to the landing point plus the frame's own size, on each axis independently; this bounds the offscreen pass to the funnel's reach rather than padding it by the whole window. requirements.verification_method: capture comparison at progress 0, 0.5, 0.9 and 0.95 for both a departure and an arrival; unit test of the reach formula, the default landing point and the removal delay

Then every `[title](target)`, with a non-empty title free of square brackets, a target without whitespace, and optionally whitespace and a double-quoted title attribute before the closing parenthesis, becomes the target alone when title and target are equal, otherwise `title (target)`. source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/LinkParagraphView.swift:226-245 `enum MarkdownLinkOpener { static func open(_ url: URL) { ... } }`

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/LinkParagraphView.swift:228-232 - `guard url.scheme == nil, url.host == nil, url.query == nil, url.fragment == nil, url.path.hasPrefix("/") else { NSWorkspace.shared.open(url); return }`

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/LinkParagraphView.swift:234-242 - when the local-file branch is taken: `var path = url.path`; if that path does not exist AND it ends in a colon followed by a positive integer, the substring up to that colon is checked; if IT exists and is not a directory, path is replaced with the stripped substring; either way, `NSWorkspace.shared.open(URL(fileURLWithPath: path))` runs last
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/LinkParagraphView.swift:92, :96 - clickedOnLink's two call sites (PR-THEME-145)
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/LinkPopover.swift:89 - the popover's Open Link row (PR-THEME-147)
requirements.preconditions: None; a pure function of one URL.
requirements.action: Any caller opens a markdown link.
requirements.expected_result: A URL with a scheme, a host, a query or a fragment always goes straight to NSWorkspace.shared.open(url) unchanged: the local-file branch requires ALL FOUR of scheme, host, query and fragment to be absent AND the path to start with "/". When that gate passes, the function tries the path as given first; only when a file does not exist at that exact path does it look for a trailing ":<positive integer>" suffix (found via the LAST colon in the string), and only when the substring before that colon both exists on disk and is not a directory does it use the stripped substring instead. In every other combination (path exists as given; no colon; the colon-prefix does not exist; the colon-prefix is a directory; the suffix is not a positive integer, including ":0" and a negative number) the original path is used unchanged. The final call is always `NSWorkspace.shared.open(URL(fileURLWithPath: path))` for the local-file branch, which silently does nothing observable to the caller if that file does not exist either.
side_effects: Opens a file with its default application, or hands the URL to the system's default handler
failure_cases: A local-file-shaped path where nothing exists at either candidate: NSWorkspace.shared.open is still called and fails silently; no error is surfaced
requirements.windows_path: UNRESOLVED pending OWNER decision O4. On Windows, `/x/a.swift:12` has no drive letter, so it is not how a user or a model would ever write an absolute Windows path; a genuine absolute path (`C:\...`, `C:/...`) parses with scheme "C" and takes the generic-opener branch, which ShellExecuteW cannot resolve correctly. Recommendation B (decisions_draft.md O4): also treat `C:\...`/`C:/...`/`/C:/...` as the local-file branch with the same `:<line>` stripping rule; never take a UNC path (`\\host\share`, `file://host/...`) down the local-file branch or the generic opener, as a named safety deviation (it would send the user's Windows credentials to a host named in model output); and for a locally runnable file type, reveal it selected in File Explorer rather than launching it, also a named safety deviation.
requirements.verification_method: unit: a table test over the four gating fields (scheme/host/query/fragment) each individually present; the exists/does-not-exist matrix for the path and its colon-stripped candidate; :0, a negative suffix, a non-numeric suffix and a directory-prefix all left unstripped
requirements.b3_note: New static helper at B3 (LinkParagraphView.swift:226-245), the routing target of PR-THEME-145 (clickedOnLink) and PR-THEME-147 (the link popover's Open Link row). Given its own atomic id so its decision procedure is testable once, independent of its three call sites. From impacts.json R3-52's new_records_needed, not folded per B3_PLAN 6.3.

requirements.title: Token counts are compacted to B, M and k with one decimal and a stripped .0
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Usage/UsagePanel.swift:110-119 static func tokens(_ count: Int) -> String { func compact(_ value: Double, _ suffix: String) -> String { let text = String(format: "%.1f", value); return (text.hasSuffix(".0") ? String(text.dropLast(2)) : text) + suffix }; if count >= 1_000_000_000 { return compact(Double(count) / 1_000_000_000, "B") }; if count >= 1_000_000 { return compact(Double(count) / 1_000_000, "M") }; if count >= 1_000 { return compact(Double(count) / 1_000, "k") }; return "\(count)" }
requirements.preconditions: A token count is being displayed.
requirements.expected_result: count >= 1000000000 gives a value in billions with suffix "B"; >= 1000000 gives millions with "M"; >= 1000 gives thousands with lowercase "k"; anything below 1000 is the plain integer with no suffix. The compact form is formatted with one decimal place and a trailing ".0" is removed, so 1000 gives "1k", 1500 gives "1.5k", 1200000 gives "1.2M". There is no space between number and suffix. Negative counts fall through to the plain branch.
failure_cases: String(format: "%.1f") rounds half to even in the C library; reproduce with a one-decimal fixed formatter and accept the same boundary results.
requirements.windows_path: Pure function; toFixed(1) with a trailing ".0" strip. Must not use a locale-aware compact number formatter, which would produce "1.2K" or a different separator.

"in \(hours) hr \(minutes) min" : "in \(max(1, minutes)) min" }; if seconds < 6 * 86_400 { return date.formatted(.dateTime.weekday(.abbreviated).hour().minute()) }; return date.formatted(.dateTime.month(.abbreviated).day()) }

requirements.action: resetText(date) is evaluated against the current time.
requirements.expected_result: The interval is clamped at zero, so a past date reads as "in 1 min". Under 86400 seconds: with whole hours greater than zero, "in <h> hr <m> min" where h is seconds/3600 and m is (seconds%3600)/60, both integer division, and m may be 0 giving for example "in 4 hr 0 min"; with zero hours, "in <m> min" where m is at least 1, so it never reads "in 0 min". Under 6*86400 seconds: the abbreviated weekday with hour and minute, for example "Sun 17:00". Otherwise: the abbreviated month and day, for example "Oct 4". The prefix "in " is part of the first branch only; the caller adds the word "Resets " or "Expires ".

requirements.title: Money is formatted with the provider's currency pinned to en_US, falling back to a plain two-decimal number
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderCredits.swift:38-45 static func money(_ value: Double, currency: String) -> String { let code = currency.uppercased(); guard code.count == 3, code.allSatisfy(\.isLetter) else { let number = plain(value); return currency.isEmpty ? number : "\(number) \(currency)" }; return value.formatted(.currency(code: code).locale(Locale(identifier: "en_US"))) }

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderCredits.swift:47-49 private static func plain(_ value: Double) -> String { value.formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(2)).locale(Locale(identifier: "en_US"))) }
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderCredits.swift:34-37 doc comment - the Mac's own locale would read "US$ 0,43" where DeepSeek's dashboard, and the rest of this app, write "$0.43"
requirements.preconditions: An amount is being formatted.
requirements.expected_result: When the uppercased currency is exactly three letters, the value is formatted as that currency in the en_US locale, giving for example "$0.43" for USD. Otherwise the value is formatted as a plain number with exactly two fraction digits in en_US, and, when the currency string is non-empty, a single space and the raw currency string are appended. An empty currency gives the bare number. The user's own locale is never consulted.
failure_cases: A currency code of the wrong length or containing digits falls back rather than showing a wrong symbol.
requirements.windows_path: Intl.NumberFormat with the fixed locale "en-US"; never the system locale. Verify the currency style output matches macOS for at least USD and CNY.

requirements.title: Each rollout contributes its own growth, its total parsed leniently through JSONValue.int: numeric strings accepted, booleans rejected, out-of-range doubles trap
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Store/TokenLedger.swift:538-572 tailContribution(at:) - seeks to the last 131072 bytes, decodes lines in reverse looking for a line containing "token_count", requires info["total_token_usage"]?["total_tokens"]?.int greater than zero, takes the day from the event's timestamp, and returns (max(0, tokens - inheritedTotal(at: url)), day); a line whose timestamp is missing or unparsable is skipped

DroppyCode/Services/Store/TokenLedger.swift:498-533 inheritedTotal(at:) - reads up to 8388608 bytes from the head in 524288 byte chunks, scanning line by line for the first token_count event, and returns max(0, total - last), or 0 when none is found; both totals read through JSONValue.int

requirements.preconditions: A rollout file is being read.

JSONValue.int accepts a JSON integer as itself, a JSON string by Int(string) parsing (so a numeric-string total like "12345" is accepted), and a JSON double by Int(value) when the double is finite (which traps at runtime for a double outside Int's range); a JSON boolean, null, array or object gives nil and the line is skipped as unparsable, same as before. From the tail's total, the file's inherited history is subtracted: the head of at most 8388608 bytes is scanned forward for the first such line and its total less its last_token_usage.total_tokens (also read through JSONValue.int, defaulting to 0 when absent or unparsable), floored at zero, is the inherited amount. The result is the file's own growth, floored at zero, attributed to the day of the tail event. A file with no qualifying line contributes nothing. For an ordinary integer total, behaviour is identical to a plain integer decode.

A resumed thread's later file therefore counts only what it added, never the history it replayed.

requirements.title: A chord another command already holds is refused with that command's own title
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Shortcuts.swift:330-333 `if let owner = AppShortcut.allCases.first(where: { $0 != shortcut && self.chord(for: $0) == chord }) { return "\(owner.title) already uses this chord." }; return nil`
requirements.preconditions: The user is recording a chord for one command.
requirements.action: They press a chord another command currently holds, whether by default or by override.
requirements.expected_result: The recording is refused with the owning command's title followed by exactly " already uses this chord.", for example "Toggle terminal already uses this chord.". The owner is the FIRST match in the enum's declaration order, so with two commands somehow holding the same chord the earlier one is named. The comparison is against live chords, so a command whose chord was cleared owns nothing and never blocks. This is the fifth and last check; passing it means the chord is accepted.
requirements.windows_path: Same search order and the same message template, using the same nineteen command titles.
requirements.verification_method: string fixture; unit on the declaration-order tie-break

requirements.title: Command-1 to Command-9 are taken in the main window before menu dispatch, and the event is swallowed
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Window/ThreadWindow.swift:5-19 the comment 'Command-1 to Command-9, taken before the event is dispatched. AppKit hands a chord that a menu item carries to the item without asking the window, and firing the item flashes its menu title, which holds the main thread for a tenth of a second on every switch.' and the monitor body `guard let self, event.window === self, attachedSheet == nil, event.modifierFlags.intersection(KeyChord.allowedModifiers) == .command, let number = Self.digitKeyCodes[event.keyCode], let selectThreadNumber else { return event }; selectThreadNumber(number); return nil`
DroppyCode/App/Window/ThreadWindow.swift:22-23 `private static let digitKeyCodes: [UInt16: Int] = [18: 1, 19: 2, 20: 3, 21: 4, 23: 5, 22: 6, 26: 7, 28: 8, 25: 9]`
DroppyCode/App/Window/WindowManager.swift:64-65 the main window's selectThread and selectThreadNumber closures are wired to model.selectThread(offset:) and model.selectThread(number:)
requirements.preconditions: The main window is key, no sheet is attached to it, and the digit closure has been installed.
requirements.action: The user presses Command and a number-row digit from 1 to 9.
requirements.expected_result: The nth thread in the sidebar's order is selected and the event is consumed, so the matching menu item never fires and its title never flashes. Every one of the five conditions is required: the event must belong to this window, no sheet may be attached, the masked modifier set must be exactly Command and nothing else, the key code must be one of the nine, and the closure must be installed. Failing any of them the event is returned unchanged and follows its normal route. Note the key code map's crossover: 23 is digit 5 and 22 is digit 6.
requirements.windows_path: A pre-translate keyboard hook on the main window that runs before accelerator dispatch, testing VK_1..VK_9 (not the numpad) with the masked modifier set exactly equal to Ctrl. It must consume the message so the menu command does not also fire. The macOS reason for the interception (a flashing menu title costing a tenth of a second) may not apply, but the double-fire it prevents does.

requirements.expected_result: If the chord matches the live next-thread chord the selection moves down one; if it matches the previous-thread chord it moves up one; either way the event is consumed. The window handles this ONLY for key code 48 (Tab): a user who rebinds next thread to a non-Tab chord falls through to the ordinary menu route instead. The chords are read live from the shortcut store, so a remap of a Tab chord is honored here too. Next is tested before previous, so if both are bound to the same chord next wins.

requirements.title: A window drag region is a transparent, full-rect SwiftUI gesture that moves the window and allows the activating click
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift:1089-1099 the doc comment 'Lets a stretch of chrome move the window, the way the sidebar does in Droppy.' and `struct WindowDragArea: View { var body: some View { Color.clear.contentShape(.rect).gesture(WindowDragGesture()).allowsWindowActivationEvents(true) } }`

porting/port_impacts.md entry 165 (G7): 'Drag strip: accept the window-activating click, start a window move on button-down, and swallow button-up so the release never reaches the UI behind it.' (the B2-era mechanism this record now supersedes; B3's WindowDragGesture is Apple's own gesture, whose press/release semantics are not documented, per 6.1 E6)
requirements.preconditions: A drag region is drawn over a stretch of chrome.
requirements.action: The user presses and releases on it.
requirements.expected_result: SwiftUI's WindowDragGesture drags the window; allowsWindowActivationEvents(true) means the gesture recognises even the click that activates an inactive window, so dragging still works from an inactive state. Apple's own documentation does not say whether the move starts on press or only after a movement threshold, nor whether a bare click or a double-click does anything (6.1 E6, oracle O-68); this is UNRESOLVED and cannot be settled without a Mac (OD-0001). Do not assume 'press immediately begins a move' or 'release is swallowed' as fixed facts any more; both are now WindowDragGesture's own behaviour, not this app's.
requirements.windows_path: ED-063's parked choice: collapse the whole drag region into one transparent, full-rect control that keeps the ED-063 WM_NCHITTEST/HTCAPTION caption region, with the system move loop giving: press-and-move drags; the activating click on an inactive window drags (matching allowsWindowActivationEvents' stated intent); the release goes to the system; double-click maximizes or restores and right-click shows the system menu, both already measured and accepted by ED-063. Keep a BeginMoveDrag fallback for windows where the caption result does not apply. If O-68 later shows macOS does not zoom on double-click, swallow WM_NCLBUTTONDBLCLK for these regions in the ED-063 hook.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test from an inactive window, and a double-click test once O-68 is settled; carries [Trait("Oracle","O-68")] on the press-start and double-click assertions

requirements.preconditions: A chrome control sits inside the 44-point title bar band.
requirements.action: The user presses, drags, releases, or right-clicks on the control.
requirements.expected_result: The window does not move. Every one of the five mouse events is forwarded to the superview, which routes it to the control under the pointer exactly as a direct dispatch would, so gestures, popovers, buttons and context menus all work. requirements.windows_path: Platform boundary: the caption hit test must return a client hit over every chrome control's bounds and HTCAPTION over the gaps between them. This is the inverse region of the drag strip and is the single most likely place for a Windows port to get the title bar wrong.
